paras.en: Huang resigned this week as Nvidia's CEO after damning reports that he had an affair with Alice Huang, who was an executive of Megaspeed, a cloud-computing company that is being eyed for possible facilitation of sending billions of dollars worth of Nvidia chips in violation of U.S. restrictions on those chips.
paras.zh: 本周，黄仁勋辞去了英伟达首席执行官的职务，此前有报道称，黄仁勋与云计算公司 Megaspeed 的高管爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 有染，该公司正被视为可能违反美国对这些芯片的限制，协助发送价值数十亿美元的英伟达芯片。

paras.en: The scandal has rocked Nvidia and raised questions about whether the Commerce Department, which is led by Howard Lutnick, has been aggressive enough at blocking advanced chips from ending up in China.
paras.zh: 这一丑闻震惊了英伟达，并引发了人们对霍华德·卢特尼克领导的商务部在阻止先进芯片进入中国方面是否足够积极的质疑。

paras.en: During Friday's call, a reporter asked why Musk was going on the trip with Trump.
paras.zh: 在周五的电话会议中，一名记者询问马斯克为什么要与特朗普一起旅行。

paras.en: "I don't want to speak for the president on exactly why Elon's going," an official said.
paras.zh: 一位官员表示：“我不想代表总统解释埃隆离职的具体原因。”

paras.en: "Obviously, he has tremendous business interests in the U.S.-China relationship. He's a big part of our national security," the official said. "There are numerous reasons, given the engagement that the president is going to have, where I think Elon would be of tremendous benefit, just even as an advisor to the president."
paras.zh: 这位官员表示：“显然，他在美中关系中拥有巨大的商业利益。他是我们国家安全的重要组成部分。” “考虑到总统将会参与其中，我认为埃隆将带来巨大的好处，即使作为总统的顾问，有很多原因。”

articles.title: FAA lifts ground stop after more than four hours, but flight cancellations will stretch into the weekend

paras.en: The U.S. halted flight departures across the country for hours on Friday for the second time since 9/11, blaming aging technology that was overloaded, affecting key information for multiple air traffic control centers.
paras.zh: 周五，美国自 9/11 事件以来第二次将全国航班起飞暂停数小时，原因是技术老化、超载，影响了多个空中交通管制中心的关键信息。

paras.en: More than 10,000 flights were disrupted during the nationwide ground stop, and delays and cancellations were set to stretch into the weekend, if not longer.
paras.zh: 在全国范围内的地面停留期间，超过 10,000 架航班受到干扰，延误和取消预计将持续到周末，甚至更长时间。

paras.en: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said at a press conference late Friday that that telecommunications routers were overloaded with data. "They went down," he said.
paras.zh: 交通部长肖恩·达菲（Sean Duffy）在周五晚间的新闻发布会上表示，电信路由器数据超载。 “他们倒下了，”他说。

paras.en: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said Friday at the White House that there was no indication that the issues were a threat to the United States. He later said at a press conference that it doesn't appear to be a cyber attack, and that it "appears this was mechanically driven."
paras.zh: 国土安全部部长马克韦恩·穆林周五在白宫表示，没有迹象表明这些问题对美国构成威胁。他后来在新闻发布会上表示，这似乎不是网络攻击，而且“这似乎是机械驱动的”。

paras.en: The Federal Aviation Administration canceled the ground stop at 8:15 p.m. ET Friday after it lasted formore than four hours and disrupted the travel plans of hundreds of thousands of travelers, including some sports teams.
paras.zh: 美国联邦航空管理局取消了晚上 8 点 15 分的地面停留。美国东部时间周五，这场风浪持续了四个多小时，扰乱了包括一些运动队在内的数十万旅客的旅行计划。

paras.en: The agency earlier said in post on X that there was a "temporary telecommunications outage" and that it halted flights out of an "abundance of caution."
paras.zh: 该机构此前在X上发帖称，发生了“临时性电信中断”，并出于“谨慎起见”暂停了航班。

paras.en: When it issued the ground stop at about 4 p.m., the FAA said the communications issues were "impacting multiple Air Route Traffic Control Centers." These facilities guide airplanes at high altitudes along their routes.
paras.zh: 当下午 4 点左右发布地面停车令时，美国联邦航空局表示，通信问题“影响了多个空中航线交通控制中心”。这些设施引导飞机在高空沿航线飞行。

paras.en: While the FAA lifted the ground stop, travel chaos continued at airports, which were forced to find places for parked planes. Delays were set to continue even as flights start taking off again.
paras.zh: 尽管美国联邦航空局取消了地面禁令，但机场的出行混乱仍在继续，机场被迫寻找停放飞机的地方。即使航班再次起飞，延误仍将继续。

paras.en: Carriers canceled more flights as the disruption wore on. JetBlue Airways told staff it would cancel the remainder of the day's flights, aside from European routes, as well as others scheduled for Saturday so that crews and planes are in place to resume operations, according to a memo seen by CNBC.
paras.zh: Carriers canceled more flights as the disruption wore on.据 CNBC 看到的一份备忘录，捷蓝航空告诉员工，除了欧洲航线以及周六的其他航班外，该公司将取消当天剩余的航班，以便机组人员和飞机就位以恢复运营。

paras.en: A ground stop halts flights at their departure point. Disruptions tend to snowball if ground stops drag on as flight crews reach their maximum number of duty hours for a day.
paras.zh: 地面站会在出发点停止航班。当机组人员达到一天的最大工作时间时，如果地面停留拖延下去，干扰就会像滚雪球一样越滚越大。

paras.en: There were 11,000 flights scheduled to depart U.S. airports after 4 p.m. ET on Friday, according to flight-data firm Cirium, with 1.5 million passengers. There were about 600 diverted flights on Friday, 104 of them sent to other airports, Cirium said.
paras.zh: 下午 4 点之后有 11,000 架航班计划从美国机场起飞。根据航班数据公司 Cirium 的数据，美国东部时间周五有 150 万名乘客。 Cirium 表示，周五约有 600 架航班改道，其中 104 架飞往其他机场。

paras.en: International flights had started taking off from coastal hubs before 6 p.m. ET.
paras.zh: 国际航班于下午 6 点前开始从沿海枢纽起飞。等。

paras.en: The FAA said earlier in the night that flights will be allowed to depart as en route traffic facilities recover, "through coordination with the air traffic control system."
paras.zh: 美国联邦航空局当晚早些时候表示，“通过与空中交通管制系统的协调”，随着航路交通设施的恢复，航班将被允许起飞。

paras.en: The FAA's technicians are investigating, the agency said.
paras.zh: 美国联邦航空局表示，该机构的技术人员正在调查。

paras.en: Nationwide ground stops are extremely rare. In January 2023, the FAA halted flights because of issues with a pilot alert system. Before that, traffic was halted nationwide after the Sept. 11, 2001, terror attacks.
paras.zh: 全国范围内的地面停留极为罕见。 2023 年 1 月，由于飞行员警报系统出现问题，美国联邦航空局 (FAA) 暂停了航班。此前，2001年9月11日恐怖袭击事件后，全国交通中断。

paras.en: Technical issues have repeatedly snarled air traffic in the U.S. in recent years. Aging infrastructure and staffing shortages have angered airline executives for years.
paras.zh: 近年来，技术问题一再困扰美国的空中交通。多年来，基础设施老化和人员短缺一直激怒航空公司高管。

paras.en: In September, hundreds of flights into Newark, New Jersey, and Philadelphia were canceled, delayed or diverted after a Verizon fiber cable was accidentally cut. Officials said it occurred during construction in New Jersey, severing a backup feed of key data for air traffic controllers.
paras.zh: 9 月，由于 Verizon 光缆意外切断，数百架飞往新泽西州纽瓦克和费城的航班被取消、延误或改道。官员们表示，这起事件发生在新泽西州的施工期间，导致空中交通管制员的关键数据备份被切断。

paras.en: In 2025, air traffic controllers lost contact with aircraft heading to and from Newark Liberty International Airport, an equipment failure that led to massive flight delays and raised more concerns about aging U.S. aviation infrastructure and staffing shortages.
paras.zh: 2025 年，空中交通管制员与往返纽瓦克自由国际机场的飞机失去联系，设备故障导致航班大规模延误，并引发了人们对美国航空基础设施老化和人员短缺的更多担忧。

paras.en: "It's going to continue to fail," Duffy said Friday of U.S. air traffic control infrastructure. The U.S. is in the middle of an overhaul of the technology, and Duffy urged lawmakers for more funding.
paras.zh: 达菲周五在谈到美国空中交通管制基础设施时表示：“它会继续失败。”美国正在对该技术进行彻底改革，达菲敦促立法者提供更多资金。

paras.en: Inbound international flights will be managed on a case by case basis, the FAA said.
paras.zh: 美国联邦航空局表示，入境国际航班将根据具体情况进行管理。

paras.en: The major U.S. airlines issued statements saying they would work with customers who were affected by the ground stop and encouraged travelers to check for updates.
paras.zh: 美国主要航空公司发表声明称，他们将与受地面停靠影响的乘客合作，并鼓励旅客检查最新情况。

paras.en: — CNBC's Kevin Breuninger and Phil LeBeau contributed to this article.
paras.zh: — CNBC 的 Kevin Breuninger 和 Phil LeBeau 对本文做出了贡献。

articles.title: Ecuador wants to monetize its biodiversity — while still drilling for oil

paras.en: Ecuador, known for its "megadiverse" Galapagos Islands, Amazon rainforest, Andes and Pacific coast, wants to protect its natural landscapes for years to come — but it faces a tricky balancing act.
paras.zh: 厄瓜多尔以其“多样化”的加拉帕戈斯群岛、亚马逊雨林、安第斯山脉和太平洋海岸而闻名，希望在未来几年保护其自然景观，但它面临着一个棘手的平衡问题。

paras.en: As well as preserving its nature, the South American country also plans to capitalize on its critical minerals and continue to extract oil from parts of the Amazon — both of which have led to protests from Indigenous and environmental groups.
paras.zh: 除了保护其自然环境外，这个南美国家还计划利用其关键矿产，并继续从亚马逊部分地区开采石油——这两项举措都引发了原住民和环保组织的抗议。

paras.en: One way Ecuador is planning to channel funds into its nature is via new financial tools, such as "debt-for-nature" swaps and its first sovereign green bond. It is also aiming to raise its environmental profile on the global stage by hosting the U.N.'s biodiversity summit, known as COP18, in 2028.
paras.zh: 厄瓜多尔计划将资金引入自然的一种方式是通过新的金融工具，例如“债务换自然”互换及其首个主权绿色债券。它还旨在通过于 2028 年主办联合国生物多样性峰会（即 COP18）来提高其在全球舞台上的环境形象。

paras.en: Ecuador, which uses the U.S. dollar, is no stranger to green finance. In March, IDB Invest, the private-sector arm of the Inter-American Development Bank, and Ecuadorian lender Banco Bolivariano issued a $120 million biodiversity bond to back conservation projects. The government also completed two swaps in 2023 and 2024 — deals in which a country's debt is refinanced on better terms in exchange for commitments to spend the savings on conservation. Together, they freed up about $1.1 billion for conservation in the Amazon and Galapagos Islands.
paras.zh: 使用美元的厄瓜多尔对绿色金融并不陌生。今年 3 月，美洲开发银行的私营部门 IDB Invest 和厄瓜多尔玻利瓦尔银行发行了 1.2 亿美元的生物多样性债券，以支持保护项目。政府还于 2023 年和 2024 年完成了两次互换，即以更好的条件为国家债务再融资，以换取将储蓄用于保护的承诺。他们总共腾出了约 11 亿美元用于亚马逊和加拉帕戈斯群岛的保护。

paras.en: Juan Carlos Blum, Ecuador's minister of environment and energy, said the country hopes to issue sovereign green bonds for the first time in 2027, to raise finance to protect its coastal and mountainous regions and the people whose livelihoods depend on them. The government is looking to the European Union for advice on such instruments, he said. The bloc set green bond standards in 2024.
paras.zh: 厄瓜多尔环境与能源部长胡安·卡洛斯·布鲁姆表示，该国希望在2027年首次发行主权绿色债券，筹集资金保护其沿海和山区以及以此为生的人民。他说，政府正在向欧盟寻求有关此类工具的建议。欧盟于 2024 年制定绿色债券标准。

paras.en: For Blum, one of the challenges is public awareness. "A lot of us are not aware of how we depend on nature, how we depend on the biodiversity, how vulnerable we all are towards climate," he told CNBC by video call.
paras.zh: 对于布鲁姆来说，挑战之一是公众意识。他通过视频电话告诉 CNBC：“我们很多人都没有意识到我们如何依赖自然，我们如何依赖生物多样性，以及我们对气候的脆弱性。”

paras.en: Another challenge for Ecuador, as it looks to protect its biodiversity, is its reliance on oil.
paras.zh: 厄瓜多尔在保护其生物多样性方面面临的另一个挑战是对石油的依赖。

paras.en: The country is a significant oil producer in Central and South America and in October, the government announced plans to open up new tenders for oil exploration in parts of the Amazon, according to local media reports. The news was reportedly met with criticism from Indigenous leaders, who strongly oppose the plans.
paras.zh: 据当地媒体报道，该国是中美洲和南美洲的重要石油生产国，10 月，政府宣布计划在亚马逊部分地区开展新的石油勘探招标。据报道，这一消息遭到了原住民领导人的批评，他们强烈反对该计划。

paras.en: "We are being careful on that balance between biodiversity and natural resources use, renewables or not renewables, and it's a delicate matter," Blum said. "That's my day-to-day reality, dealing with balancing this."
paras.zh: 布鲁姆说：“我们正在谨慎对待生物多样性和自然资源利用、可再生能源或不可再生能源之间的平衡，这是一个微妙的问题。” “这就是我的日常现实，处理平衡问题。”

paras.en: About 80% of Ecuador's energy was generated from oil and oil products in 2024, according to the International Energy Agency, while about two-thirds of its electricity was produced using hydroelectric power.
paras.zh: 据国际能源署称，到 2024 年，厄瓜多尔约 80% 的能源来自石油和石油产品，而约三分之二的电力来自水力发电。

paras.en: Cracking down on illegal mining is a focus for Blum, who told CNBC he was aware of the environmental impact of legal mining, but that illegal mining was a far bigger problem.
paras.zh: 打击非法采矿是布鲁姆的重点，他告诉 CNBC，他意识到合法采矿对环境的影响，但非法采矿是一个更大的问题。

paras.en: At Ecuador's first Bio Summit held Nov. 4 to Nov. 6 in Quito — an event aimed at helping the country's natural assets "enter the global financial system" — a new way of monetizing nature was introduced.
paras.zh: 厄瓜多尔首届生物峰会于 11 月 4 日至 6 日在基多举行，旨在帮助该国的自然资产“进入全球金融体系”，会上引入了一种利用自然货币化的新方式。

paras.en: Marcelo Salame, the event's president, told CNBC he is working on a project to bring so-called biodiversity credits to the country for the first time, to "preserve and monetize" a 260-hectare, or 640-acre, area of the Prosperina forest owned by ESPOL University in the port city of Guayaquil.
paras.zh: 该活动主席马塞洛·萨拉梅 (Marcelo Salame) 告诉 CNBC，他正在开展一个项目，首次将所谓的生物多样性信用引入该国，以“保护并货币化”港口城市瓜亚基尔 ESPOL 大学拥有的 260 公顷（640 英亩）Prosperina 森林区域。

paras.en: Salame said biodiversity is "multidimensional," with credits reflecting a whole ecosystem rather than carbon emissions alone.
paras.zh: 萨拉姆说，生物多样性是“多维的”，积分反映了整个生态系统，而不仅仅是碳排放。

paras.en: Biodiversity credits work in a similar way to the carbon credits that large companies buy to meet sustainability goals, but track a range of measures such as the number of species in a given area or tree canopy cover, with the money raised funneled back into nature protection.
paras.zh: 生物多样性信用额的运作方式与大公司为实现可持续发展目标而购买的碳信用额类似，但它跟踪一系列措施，例如特定区域的物种数量或树冠覆盖率，筹集的资金将重新用于自然保护。

paras.en: But whereas carbon credits can be used to offset emissions, biodiversity credits cannot. "It's all about funding verified nature outcomes and not, to date at least, compensating for damage," Martin Vaquié, co-founder of Berlin-based Bloomlabs, a company that tracks the biodiversity market, told CNBC.
paras.zh: 但是，虽然碳信用额可以用来抵消排放量，但生物多样性信用额却不能。 “这一切都是为了资助经过验证的自然成果，而不是至少到目前为止，补偿损害，”总部位于柏林的 Bloomlabs（一家跟踪生物多样性市场的公司）的联合创始人 Martin Vaquié 告诉 CNBC。

paras.en: Jerry Toth, a conservationist and co-founder of Ecuador-based Third Millennium Alliance, a nonprofit that aims to protect the "last remnants" of Ecuador's Pacific Forest, told CNBC that carbon markets can reduce the ecological value of a forest to a single metric: how many tons of carbon it stores.
paras.zh: 杰里·托特 (Jerry Toth) 是一位自然资源保护主义者，也是总部位于厄瓜多尔的第三个千年联盟 (Third Millennium Alliance) 的联合创始人，该联盟是一家致力于保护厄瓜多尔太平洋森林“最后遗迹”的非营利组织。他告诉 CNBC，碳市场可以将森林的生态价值降低到一个指标：它储存了多少吨碳。

paras.en: "That can be potentially dangerous because then you have people that are optimizing for this one metric at the expense of all the other things," he said. Toth hopes biodiversity credits can capture the nuances of an ecosystem.
paras.zh: 他说：“这可能存在潜在危险，因为人们会以牺牲所有其他指标为代价来优化这一指标。”托特希望生物多样性积分能够捕捉到生态系统的细微差别。

paras.en: Toth also runs chocolate maker To'ak — which made headlines for producing the "world's most expensive chocolate bar" — using ancient Nacional cacao grown in Ecuador's Manabí province and processed in Quito.
paras.zh: 托特还经营巧克力制造商 To'ak，该公司因生产“世界上最昂贵的巧克力棒”而成为头条新闻，该公司使用厄瓜多尔马纳比省种植的古老国家可可，并在基多加工。

paras.en: Third Millennium Alliance works with farmers to restore degraded land by planting cacao in the shade of taller trees, and To'ak pays them around $1.20 per pound of cacao, about double the current market price, Toth said.
paras.zh: 托特说，第三个千年联盟与农民合作，通过在较高的树荫下种植可可来恢复退化的土地，托阿克向他们支付每磅可可约 1.20 美元的费用，大约是当前市场价格的两倍。

paras.en: Ensuring that chocolate production does not deplete nature is "the key question," Toth said. "Our goal at the outset was, how do we use chocolate to reverse deforestation?"
paras.zh: 托特说，确保巧克力生产不会消耗自然是“关键问题”。 “我们一开始的目标是，如何利用巧克力来扭转森林砍伐？”

paras.en: Ecuador recognizes its "immense" ecological and biological resources, Toth said. "It's still trying to figure out how to … capture that value in a way that makes sense both for people in Ecuador and for the ecosystem."
paras.zh: 托特说，厄瓜多尔认识到其“巨大”的生态和生物资源。 “它仍在试图找出如何……以一种对厄瓜多尔人民和生态系统都有意义的方式捕捉这种价值。”

articles.title: The Euclid space telescope captures nearly a billion celestial objects in stunning detail

paras.en: Astronomers took a major step toward navigating the universe, thanks to the European Space Agency’s (ESA’s) Euclid space telescope, which just released its first major batch of observations.
paras.zh: 得益于欧洲航天局 (ESA) 的欧几里得太空望远镜，天文学家在探索宇宙方面迈出了重要一步，该望远镜刚刚发布了第一批主要观测数据。

paras.en: Since its launch in July 2023, Euclid has been using its approximately 600-megapixel visible-light camera to capture images of the cosmos, near and far. All told, it has already managed to document nearly a billion objects, including more than 900 million galaxies and 60 million possible quasars, the ultrabright nuclei of galaxies where ultrahot gas is being sucked into a supermassive black hole.
paras.zh: 自 2023 年 7 月推出以来，Euclid 一直在使用其约 600 兆像素的可见光相机来捕捉近处和远处的宇宙图像。总而言之，它已经成功记录了近十亿个物体，其中包括超过 9 亿个星系和 6000 万个可能的类星体，这些类星体是超亮的星系核，其中的超热气体被吸入超大质量黑洞。

paras.en: Previous releases of images by Euclid had been focused on a far narrower band of sky. Now the huge amount of data collected—more than 1.7 million gigabytes—makes the new release the “largest space-based survey of its kind, laying the foundation of future discovery in a new regime for astronomy,” said ESA’s director of science Carole Mundell in a statement.
paras.zh: 欧几里得之前发布的图像主要集中在更窄的天空带上。 ESA 科学主任卡罗尔·蒙代尔 (Carole Mundell) 在一份声明中表示，现在收集到的大量数据（超过 170 万千兆字节）使新发布的数据成为“同类中最大的太空调查，为天文学新体制中的未来发现奠定了基础”。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: Euclid is aided in its observations by a cosmic phenomenon known as gravitational lensing. As light emitted from galaxies and other celestial objects travels through space, it interacts with the gravitational forces of other large objects. That gravity bends and magnifies the light, making it brighter and easier to detect for telescopes such as Euclid; it can even allow astronomers to determine the mass of the source. But the objects must line up just right for the lensing to occur, making them extremely rare.
paras.zh: 欧几里得的观测得到了一种称为引力透镜的宇宙现象的帮助。当星系和其他天体发出的光穿过太空时，它会与其他大型物体的引力相互作用。重力会弯曲并放大光线，使其变得更亮，更容易被欧几里德等望远镜探测到；它甚至可以让天文学家确定源的质量。但这些物体必须恰好对齐才能发生透镜效应，这使得它们极其罕见。

paras.en: According to ESA, Euclid has identified around 15,000 strong candidates for gravitational lensing, a trove that Scott Gaudi, an astronomer at the Ohio State University, calls “bonkers.”
paras.zh: 据欧空局称，欧几里得已经确定了大约 15,000 个引力透镜的有力候选者，俄亥俄州立大学天文学家斯科特·高迪称这些候选者为“疯狂”。

paras.en: “Gravitational lenses are one of nature’s toolboxes for us measuring dark matter mass by looking for these distortions of background quasars and galaxies due to foreground structures,” says Gaudi, who is not involved in the Euclid program. “But you can’t do it from the ground. You just need the high-resolution imaging to do it.”
paras.zh: “引力透镜是大自然的工具箱之一，我们通过寻找前景结构导致的背景类星体和星系的扭曲来测量暗物质质量，”未参与欧几里得计划的高迪说。 “但你不能在地面上做到这一点。你只需要高分辨率成像就可以做到这一点。”

paras.en: The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, which relies on instruments that examine infrared light, as opposed to the optical light Euclid is designed for, will also harness gravitational lensing to see far-off cosmic objects. The two approaches are “very complementary,” Gaudi says, particularly when it comes to searching for elusive things such as dark energy and dark matter.
paras.zh: 南希·格雷斯·罗马太空望远镜依赖于检查红外光的仪器，而不是欧几里德设计的光学光，它也将利用引力透镜来观察遥远的宇宙物体。高迪说，这两种方法“非常互补”，特别是在寻找暗能量和暗物质等难以捉摸的事物时。

paras.en: “Euclid is going for as much area as possible, whereas Roman is focusing in the infrared, and it’s focusing on repeating observations of the same area of the sky with different roll angles and different filters,” Gaudi says. “I think the joint approach of those two missions is very powerful because you can vet the big statistics you get with Euclid with a very careful controlled system with Roman.”
paras.zh: 高迪说：“欧几里得的目标是尽可能多的区域，而罗曼则专注于红外线，它的重点是用不同的滚动角和不同的滤光片重复观察天空的同一区域。” “我认为这两个任务的联合方法非常强大，因为你可以通过与罗马一起非常仔细的控制系统来审查从欧几里得获得的大量统计数据。”

paras.en: Euclid’s latest release also includes a large amount of data on galaxy clusters. Examining how galaxies are bunched together can offer insights into how the first matter formed and organized shortly after the big bang. And Euclid can help astronomers begin to figure out where individual galaxies are located in relation to one another, leading to what could be the most comprehensive three-dimensional map of the universe ever made.
paras.zh: Euclid的最新发布还包含了大量关于星系团的数据。研究星系如何聚集在一起可以深入了解大爆炸后不久第一个物质是如何形成和组织的。欧几里得可以帮助天文学家开始弄清楚各个星系彼此之间的相对位置，从而绘制出迄今为止最全面的三维宇宙地图。

paras.en: “Euclid doesn’t just look far back in time—it does so across huge areas of sky,” said Barbara Sartoris, an astrophysicist at France’s Joseph-Louis Lagrange Laboratory, in the ESA statement. “This gives us an unprecedented view of large samples of ancient galaxy clusters that were previously out of reach. We will explore these in the coming months to learn how these giants grew, and decipher what they reveal about the dark Universe.”
paras.zh: 法国约瑟夫·路易斯·拉格朗日实验室的天体物理学家芭芭拉·萨托里斯（Barbara Sartoris）在欧洲航天局的声明中表示：“欧几里得不仅仅是回顾遥远的过去，它还跨越了广阔的天空区域。” “这让我们对以前无法到达的古代星系团的大型样本有了前所未有的了解。我们将在未来几个月内探索这些样本，以了解这些巨人是如何生长的，并破译它们揭示的关于黑暗宇宙的信息。”

articles.title: FAA grounds all U.S. flights days after expanding its AI air traffic system

paras.en: On a typical Friday November evening, millions of passengers would be hopping on flights for pre-Thanksgiving weekend trips and journeys home after work. But today on November 13, domestic and international flights throughout the U.S. completely ground to a halt at about 4 P.M. EST.
paras.zh: 在一个典型的 11 月周五晚上，数以百万计的乘客将搭乘航班进行感恩节前的周末旅行和下班后回家的旅程。但今天 11 月 13 日下午 4 点左右，美国各地的国内和国际航班完全停止。美国东部时间。

paras.en: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) cited a “temporary telecommunications outage,” in a post on X, and all flights have been grounded “out of an abundance of caution.”
paras.zh: 美国联邦航空管理局 (FAA) 在 X 上的一篇帖子中提到了“暂时的电信中断”，“出于高度谨慎”，所有航班均已停飞。

paras.en: The sweeping aviation disruption comes three days after the FAA expanded its Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes and Trajectories system, known as SMART. The FAA previously tested the system in the National Capital Region, the airspace around Washington, D.C., in September. The artificial intelligence-driven system is intended to synthesize data on weather patterns, flight paths, traffic flow and controller staffing metrics in order to “reduce delays and cancellations,” according to the FAA’s description. As of November 10, it was deployed across all 22 air traffic regions in the country.
paras.zh: 这场全面的航空中断是在美国联邦航空局扩大其空域、航线和轨迹战略管理系统（即 SMART）三天后发生的。美国联邦航空局此前于 9 月在国家首都地区（华盛顿特区周围的空域）测试了该系统。根据美国联邦航空局的描述，人工智能驱动的系统旨在综合有关天气模式、飞行路径、交通流量和管制人员配备指标的数据，以“减少延误和取消”。截至11月10日，该系统已在全国22个空中交通区域部署。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: Such nationwide groundings are exceedingly rare. The last time the FAA stopped flights was for 90 minutes on January 11, 2023, to address an outage in its Notice to Air Missions (NOTAM) system, which informs pilots and operators about potential safety hazards. Before that, flights were halted immediately following the September 11, 2001 terror attacks.
paras.zh: 这种全国范围内的停飞极为罕见。 FAA 上次停止航班是在 2023 年 1 月 11 日，时间为 90 分钟，以解决其空中任务通知 (NOTAM) 系统的中断问题，该系统向飞行员和操作员通报潜在的安全隐患。在此之前，2001 年 9 月 11 日恐怖袭击后，航班立即停止。

paras.en: The FAA Telecommunications Infrastructure is managed by L3Harris, a Silicon Valley-based aerospace and defense company and a contractor for federal government agencies. L3Harris did not immediately respond to Scientific American’s requests for comment. The FAA issued a brief statement, saying that “FAA technicians are investigating the issue. We will provide updates.”
paras.zh: FAA 电信基础设施由 L3Harris 管理，L3Harris 是一家总部位于硅谷的航空航天和国防公司，也是联邦政府机构的承包商。 L3Harris 没有立即回应《科学美国人》的置评请求。美国联邦航空局发表了一份简短声明，称“美国联邦航空局技术人员正在调查该问题。我们将提供最新情况。”

paras.en: Ruth Stilwell, a former air traffic controller and aerospace policy expert, speculates that the outage may be due to a software problem, such as a software update gone awry in the Voice Switching and Control System, which manages communications between pilots and air traffic controllers. It is not Microsoft software, Stilwell emphasizes, referring to the widespread Microsoft product outage that occurred on Thursday into Friday. CBS News reported that a software update to the private communications system may have triggered a system-wide reboot, causing it to crash.
paras.zh: 前空中交通管制员和航空航天政策专家露丝·史迪威（Ruth Stilwell）推测，这次中断可能是由于软件问题造成的，例如管理飞行员和空中交通管制员之间通信的语音切换和控制系统的软件更新出现问题。史迪威强调，这不是微软的软件，他指的是周四至周五发生的广泛的微软产品中断。哥伦比亚广播公司新闻报道称，私人通信系统的软件更新可能触发了系统范围内的重新启动，导致其崩溃。

paras.en: “It would be unusual for them to do a software update during the day, but the FAA is very short-staffed,” Stilwell says. Department of Government Efficiency-related cuts laid off hundreds of FAA workers last year.
paras.zh: “他们在白天进行软件更新是不寻常的，但联邦航空局的人手非常短缺，”史迪威说。去年，政府效率部因削减开支而解雇了数百名联邦航空局员工。

paras.en: "This is yet another example of how brittle our air transportation system is in our country," says Missy Cummings, at George Mason University and a former fighter pilot whose research focuses on responsible AI in transportation. "This has been a problem over several administration, and the Trump administration made the situation much worse with all their cuts."
paras.zh: 乔治梅森大学的米西·卡明斯 (Missy Cummings) 表示：“这是我们国家航空运输系统脆弱性的又一个例子。”她的研究重点是运输中负责任的人工智能。 “这一直是几届政府面临的问题，而特朗普政府的所有削减让情况变得更糟。”

paras.en: Even if the problem, software-related or otherwise, was small in scale, it’s standard procedure to ground planes while attempting to communicate through other channels with pilots who have already taken off, Stilwell says.
paras.zh: 史迪威说，即使与软件相关或其他方面的问题规模很小，这也是地面飞机尝试通过其他渠道与已经起飞的飞行员进行沟通时的标准程序。

paras.en: “The ground stop was the right thing to do,” Stilwell says. “Planes in the air are the top priority. The safety of those flights is way more important than anybody’s delay. The planes on the ground are safe.”
paras.zh: “地面停留是正确的做法，”史迪威说。 “空中的飞机是重中之重。这些航班的安全比任何人的延误都重要得多。地面上的飞机是安全的。”

paras.en: This is a developing story and will be updated.
paras.zh: 这是一个正在发展的故事，将会更新。

articles.title: Math Puzzle: Slippery slopes

paras.en: If five points are placed as shown here and straight lines are drawn between each pair of points, each line will have a unique slope. Almost all configurations of five points have this property.
paras.zh: 如果如图所示放置五个点并在每对点之间绘制直线，则每条线将具有唯一的斜率。几乎所有五点配置都具有此属性。

paras.en: Suppose you are allowed to intentionally place the five points anywhere as long as no three points can be contained in the same straight line. What is the smallest possible number of slopes that can be made by connecting pairs of points? How can you be sure?
paras.zh: 假设您可以故意将这五个点放置在任意位置，只要三个点不能包含在同一条直线中即可。通过连接点对可以形成的最小斜率是多少？你怎么能确定？

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: Challenge: What is the smallest possible number of slopes determined by any number of points? Can you prove it?
paras.zh: 挑战：由任意数量的点确定的最小可能的斜率是多少？你能证明吗？

paras.en: Three lines that form a triangle will always have three different slopes: if two of the lines were parallel (and thus had the same slope), they would not be able to meet up at a corner. This means the minimum number of slopes among three points that are not in a straight line is three.
paras.zh: 形成三角形的三条线始终具有三种不同的斜率：如果其中两条线平行（因此具有相同的斜率），它们将无法在角处相交。这意味着不在一条直线上的三个点之间的斜率最少为三个。

paras.en: Consider any configuration of five points in which no three points are in a line. Find the bottommost point and sweep out a line from it, recording the angles at which it hits the other points. If any two points share the same angle, they are both in a line with the lowest point, which means our arrangement of five points is invalid. Because that’s not allowed, we must have four unique slopes. Now draw a line from the first point you hit to the last. This line forms triangles with all the other lines and thus must give us a fifth slope—so the number of slopes is at least five. But is there a configuration with only five?
paras.zh: 考虑任何五个点的配置，其中没有三个点在一条线上。找到最底部的点并从中扫出一条线，记录它撞击其他点的角度。如果任意两个点具有相同的角度，则它们都与最低点在一条线上，这意味着我们的五个点的排列是无效的。因为这是不允许的，所以我们必须有四个独特的斜坡。现在从您击中的第一个点到最后一个点画一条线。这条线与所有其他线形成三角形，因此必须给我们第五个斜率 - 因此斜率的数量至少为五个。但有没有只有五个的配置？

paras.en: Consider the configuration where the five points form a regular pentagon:
paras.zh: 考虑五个点形成正五边形的配置：

paras.en: The pairs of points form lines tracing the sides of the pentagon and all of the diagonals contained within it. Each of the sides has a unique slope. Each of the diagonals is parallel to, and thus has the same slope as, one of the sides. This gives us five slopes in total.
paras.zh: 这些点对形成了追踪五边形的边以及其中包含的所有对角线的线。每条边都有独特的坡度。每条对角线均平行于其中一侧，因此具有相同的斜率。这总共给了我们五个斜坡。

paras.en: The answer for n points is n slopes, and in each case, the configuration that realizes this is a regular polygon. By the argument above, there must be at least n slopes among the n points. In an odd-sided polygon, each internal diagonal is parallel to a side, as demonstrated above. In the even-sided case, it becomes a bit more complicated. Sides come in parallel pairs, giving n⁄2 unique slopes from the polygon’s sides, and every internal diagonal is either parallel to a side or parallel to another diagonal that skips one point along the edge. There are n⁄2 unique slopes from the internal diagonals, which gives n slopes in total.
paras.zh: n 个点的答案是 n 个斜率，在每种情况下，实现这一点的配置都是正多边形。根据上面的论证，n 个点之间必须至少有 n 个斜率。在奇数边多边形中，每个内部对角线都平行于一条边，如上所示。在双方均等的情况下，情况会变得更加复杂。边成对平行，从多边形的边给出 n⁄2 个独特的斜率，并且每个内部对角线要么平行于一条边，要么平行于沿着边缘跳过一个点的另一条对角线。从内部对角线开始有 n⁄2 个独特的斜率，总共给出 n 个斜率。

paras.en: We’d love to hear from you! E-mail us at games@sciam.com to share your experience. if you can't see the puzzle answer reveal above, visit this page in a web browser.
paras.zh: 我们很乐意听取您的意见！请发送电子邮件至 games@sciam.com 与我们分享您的经验。如果您看不到上面显示的谜题答案，请在网络浏览器中访问此页面。

articles.title: Fossil fuel emissions are down in 2026. Green energy isn’t the reason
articles.author: Nikk Ogasa

paras.en: This is a human-written story voiced by AI. Got feedback?
paras.zh: 这是一个由人工智能配音的人类书写的故事。有反馈吗？

paras.en: Scientists project that global carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuels will decrease by 0.4 percent this year, after having grown by 0.8 percent each year on average from 2019 to 2025.
paras.zh: 科学家预测，全球化石燃料二氧化碳排放量在 2019 年至 2025 年平均每年增长 0.8% 后，今年将减少 0.4%。

paras.en: But the dip may not last. The lower emissions are probably driven by high oil prices stemming from the Iran war, researchers report November 9 in Nature Climate Change.
paras.zh: 但这种下滑可能不会持续下去。研究人员 11 月 9 日在《自然·气候变化》杂志上报告称，排放量下降可能是由伊朗战争引发的高油价推动的。

paras.en: Global emissions probably would have grown again this year without the energy shock of the Iran war, says Glen Peters, a climate scientist at the Center for International Climate Research in Oslo, Norway. “So the energy transition that’s happening … it’s not quite big enough to get emissions heading downward yet.”
paras.zh: 挪威奥斯陆国际气候研究中心的气候科学家格伦·彼得斯表示，如果没有伊朗战争的能源冲击，今年全球排放量可能会再次增长。 “所以正在发生的能源转型……还没有大到足以使排放量下降。”

paras.en: For the study, Peters and his colleagues used data on countries’ electric vehicle stocks and wind and solar energy generation to project those technologies impacts on global fossil CO2 emissions through 2028. The team used the generative AI model Claude to source data and write code for analysis.
paras.zh: 在这项研究中，Peters 和他的同事使用了各国电动汽车库存以及风能和太阳能发电的数据来预测这些技术对 2028 年全球化石二氧化碳排放的影响。该团队使用生成式人工智能模型 Claude 来获取数据并编写代码进行分析。

paras.en: By year’s end, global emissions will reach 38.24 gigatons, the researchers found, which is about 0.16 gigatons less than were emitted in 2025. For comparison, annual global emissions fell by nearly two gigatons in 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic and by about 0.5 gigatons in 2009 because of the global financial crisis.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现，到年底，全球排放量将达到 38.24 吉吨，比 2025 年的排放量减少约 0.16 吉吨。相比之下，由于 COVID-19 大流行，2020 年全球年排放量减少了近 2 吉吨，由于全球金融危机，2009 年全球年排放量减少了约 0.5 吉吨。

paras.en: If electric vehicle sales and solar and wind capacity continue growing at the rates they did in 2026, those technologies should counteract about 63 percent of the growth in emissions from 2025 to 2028 — or help avoid about 1.64 gigatons of added emissions.
paras.zh: 如果电动汽车销量以及太阳能和风能装机容量继续以 2026 年的速度增长，这些技术将抵消 2025 年至 2028 年排放量增长的约 63%，或者有助于避免约 1.64 吉吨的新增排放量。

paras.en: The results indicate that the energy transition needs to accelerate if humankind is to realize consistently declining emissions, though EVs, solar and wind are already having a large impact. Without the offset in emissions provided by those technologies, global emissions would have risen by 1.9 percent each year on average from 2019 to 2025, the researchers note.
paras.zh: 结果表明，尽管电动汽车、太阳能和风能已经产生了巨大影响，但如果人类要实现排放量持续下降，就需要加速能源转型。研究人员指出，如果没有这些技术带来的排放抵消，2019 年至 2025 年全球排放量将平均每年增加 1.9%。

paras.en: It’s very hard to say exactly how long it will take for humanity to reach peak emissions, Peters says. However, he notes, “the fact that we’re talking about this means that we’re close to that point.”
paras.zh: 彼得斯说，很难确切地说人类需要多长时间才能达到排放峰值。然而，他指出，“我们正在谈论这个事实意味着我们已经接近这一点。”

articles.title: Light is hard to block from every direction. This physicist found a way
articles.author: Emily Conover

paras.en: This is a human-written story voiced by AI. Got feedback?
paras.zh: 这是一个由人工智能配音的人类书写的故事。有反馈吗？

paras.en: Physicist Stefano Martiniani has designed an entirely new class of materials that blurs the line between order and chaos. Called gyromorphs, these metamaterials rely on crystal-like geometric structure and liquidlike randomness to block light from penetrating at any angle.
paras.zh: 物理学家 Stefano Martiniani 设计了一种全新的材料，模糊了秩序与混乱之间的界限。这些超材料被称为陀螺仪，依靠类晶体的几何结构和类液体的随机性来阻止光线以任何角度穿透。

paras.en: Physicists thought, structurally speaking, that they could not create such hybrid materials. “But this is evidence that you can, under certain constraints,” says Martiniani, of New York University. He likens the gyromorphs’ disorderliness to a crowd of people. You could see through the crowd if individuals stood still in straight lines, but not if they are clustered together in random groups. But there’s order too: From anywhere you stand in a gyromorph crowd, you’ll see a ring of people at a given distance.
paras.zh: 物理学家认为，从结构上来说，他们无法制造出这种混合材料。纽约大学的马蒂尼亚尼说：“但这证明在某些限制下你可以做到。”他将陀螺怪的混乱状态比作一群人。如果人们站成一条直线，你可以透过人群看到，但如果他们随机聚集在一起，你就看不到。但也有秩序：无论你站在旋转人群中的任何地方，你都会看到在一定距离内有一圈人。

paras.en: Gyromorphs are a type of metamaterial, a substance with a structure designed to give it properties not found in naturally occurring materials. Metamaterials can control light, sound or other waves, and are often used in smartphones, medical imaging and computers. Martiniani says gyromorphs could be used to make more energy-efficient optical computers, which use light to process and store data.
paras.zh: 回旋体是一种超材料，这种物质的结构旨在赋予其天然材料所没有的特性。超材料可以控制光、声或其他波，通常用于智能手机、医学成像和计算机。马蒂尼亚尼表示，陀螺仪可用于制造更节能的光学计算机，该计算机利用光来处理和存储数据。

paras.en: To design a gyromorph, Martiniani needed to find a way to achieve the perfect structural balance. He turned to FReSCo, a program his lab created that designs molecular structures to meet researchers’ specifications, for help. “We had an algorithm, we gave it an objective, and then it was able to solve that objective, finding a solution that we were not expecting,” he says. “That is the best kind of discovery.”
paras.zh: 为了设计陀螺模型，马蒂尼亚尼需要找到一种方法来实现完美的结构平衡。他向 FReSCo 寻求帮助，这是他的实验室创建的一个程序，用于设计分子结构以满足研究人员的规格。 “我们有一个算法，我们给它一个目标，然后它能够​​解决这个目标，找到一个我们没有预料到的解决方案，”他说。 “这是最好的发现。”

articles.title: This magic mushroom can kill
articles.author: Tina Hesman Saey

paras.en: People who eat this tiny magic mushroom may hit a lethal low instead of getting high.
paras.zh: 吃了这种微小的神奇蘑菇的人可能会陷入致命的低谷，而不是变得兴奋。

paras.en: The fungus makes hallucinogenic psilocybin and deadly amatoxin, researchers report November 11 in Current Biology. Dubbed “dark magic mushrooms,” it is the first species of fungus discovered to make both types of compounds.
paras.zh: 研究人员 11 月 11 日在《当代生物学》杂志上报道称，这种真菌会产生致幻性裸盖菇素和致命的鹅膏毒素。它被称为“黑魔法蘑菇”，是第一种被发现能产生这两种化合物的真菌。

paras.en: Chemist and fungal biologist Andrew Kunik found the dark magic mushroom in 2025 growing on a decaying moss-covered palm trunk in a central Florida wetland. Kunik, who was then doing post-baccalaureate research in the lab of fungal biologist Matthew Smith at the University of Florida in Gainesville, identified the mini mushroom as Galerina indica.
paras.zh: 化学家兼真菌生物学家安德鲁·库尼克 (Andrew Kunik) 于 2025 年在佛罗里达州中部湿地的一棵腐烂的长满青苔的棕榈树干上发现了这种黑魔法蘑菇。库尼克当时正在盖恩斯维尔佛罗里达大学真菌生物学家马修·史密斯的实验室进行学士学位后研究，他将这种迷你蘑菇鉴定为 Galerina indica。

paras.en: That species had not been reported in Florida before, Kunik says. “It’s quite rare and unusual.” He also found two other new related species, tagged with the placeholder names Galerina species 1 and Galerina species 2.
paras.zh: 库尼克说，佛罗里达州以前从未报道过该物种。 “这是非常罕见和不寻常的。”他还发现了另外两个新的相关物种，并用占位符名称 Galerina 物种 1 和 Galerina 物种 2 进行了标记。

paras.en: Other researchers had previously described G. indica’s appearance and found DNA signatures that distinguish the fungus from related species. But no one had cataloged the mushroom’s complete chemical or genetic makeup.
paras.zh: 其他研究人员此前曾描述过 G. indica 的外观，并发现了将这种真菌与相关物种区分开来的 DNA 特征。但没有人对这种蘑菇的完整化学或基因组成进行分类。

paras.en: Related Galerina species make amatoxins, deadly chemicals that can kill in even tiny amounts and are found in death cap mushrooms and other species. Kunik and colleagues looked for those toxins in G. indica and the two other new Galerina species. G. indica makes a previously undiscovered form of amatoxin the team is calling alpha-proamanitin, the chemical analysis revealed.
paras.zh: 相关的 Galerina 物种会产生鹅膏毒素，这是一种致命的化学物质，即使微量也能致人死亡，死帽蘑菇和其他物种中也存在这种毒素。 Kunik 和同事在 G. indica 和另外两个新的 Galerina 物种中寻找这些毒素。化学分析显示，G. indica 会产生一种以前未被发现的鹅膏毒素，该团队将其称为 α-鹅膏毒原。

paras.en: The small mushroom also had blue bruises, a clue that it might make psilocybin, a psychedelic chemical being tested as a treatment for mental health disorders. Fungi usually make either amatoxin or psilocybin. Not both. Galerina species 1 also makes psilocybin but doesn’t make amatoxin, and species 2 makes neither.
paras.zh: 这种小蘑菇也有蓝色的瘀伤，这表明它可能会产生裸盖菇素，一种迷幻化学物质，正在测试用于治疗精神健康障碍。真菌通常产生鹅膏毒素或裸盖菇素。两者都不是。 Galerina 物种 1 也产生裸盖菇素，但不产生鹅膏毒素，而物种 2 则两者都不产生。

paras.en: “This finding shows that there’s a lot more diversity in [fungal] chemistry and the ways that they’re combined than we had really thought about,” says Anne Pringle, a mycologist at the University of Wisconsin–Madison who was not involved in the work.
paras.zh: “这一发现表明，[真菌]化学及其组合方式的多样性比我们真正想象的要多得多，”威斯康星大学麦迪逊分校的真菌学家安妮·普林格尔（Anne Pringle）说，她没有参与这项工作。

paras.en: Discovering these dual compounds in one mushroom was both exciting and required further analysis to confirm, Kunik says. “Surprising discoveries require great depth of evidence,” he says.
paras.zh: 库尼克说，在一种蘑菇中发现这些双重化合物既令人兴奋，又需要进一步分析来证实。 “令人惊讶的发现需要大量深入的证据，”他说。

paras.en: A complete workup of the mushroom’s DNA revealed genes for producing both types of chemicals. Ancestors of these dark magic mushrooms probably picked up those genes by swapping DNA with other species. Such DNA swapping, called horizontal gene transfer, is one way that organisms can quickly evolve new traits, like when bacteria exchange antibiotic resistance genes with unrelated species.
paras.zh: 对蘑菇 DNA 的完整分析揭示了产生这两种化学物质的基因。这些黑魔法蘑菇的祖先可能通过与其他物种交换 DNA 获得了这些基因。这种 DNA 交换被称为水平基因转移，是生物体快速进化出新性状的一种方式，就像细菌与不相关物种交换抗生素抗性基因一样。

paras.en: Ancestors of G. indica and its relatives probably acquired amatoxin genes early on. Those toxins are made by many of G. indica’s cousins, which indicates that amatoxins are probably heirlooms passed down from common ancestors. Ancestors of species 1 and species 2 seem to have dropped the amatoxin genes at some point since they no longer make the compounds.
paras.zh: G. indica 及其近亲的祖先很可能很早就获得了鹅膏毒素基因。这些毒素是由许多 G. indica 的表亲产生的，这表明鹅膏毒素可能是从共同祖先遗传下来的传家宝。物种 1 和物种 2 的祖先似乎在某个时候已经放弃了鹅膏毒素基因，因为它们不再制造这些化合物。

paras.en: The two psilocybin-producing species may have independently obtained the psychedelic genes in separate DNA swap meets, or a common ancestor may have picked up the genes and then passed them down to G. indica and species 1. There’s not enough known about the fungi’s family tree to sort out which scenario is correct.
paras.zh: 这两个产生裸盖菇素的物种可能在不同的 DNA 交换中独立获得了致幻基因，或者共同的祖先可能获得了这些基因，然后将它们传递给 G. indica 和物种 1。对真菌的家谱还没有足够的了解，无法确定哪种情况是正确的。

paras.en: And there’s another unsolved evolutionary mystery, Pringle says. “We still don’t know why mushrooms are poisonous.” Many scientists think it is for defending against predators, but hard evidence is lacking, she says.
paras.zh: 普林格尔说，还有另一个未解的进化之谜。 “我们仍然不知道为什么蘑菇有毒。”她说，许多科学家认为这是为了防御掠食者，但缺乏确凿的证据。

paras.en: “Can I eat it?” is often the first question people ask when finding a new mushroom, Pringle says. “I’m always so uncomfortable with that question and that conversation. And this paper confirms that, in fact, you should be uncomfortable.” After all, eating these dark magic mushrooms could send people tripping into the grave.
paras.zh: “Can I eat it?”普林格尔说，这通常是人们在寻找新蘑菇时提出的第一个问题。 “我总是对这个问题和谈话感到不舒服。这篇论文证实，事实上，你应该感到不舒服。”毕竟，吃了这些黑魔法蘑菇可能会让人绊倒进坟墓。

articles.title: Physicists Find a Mathematical Limit to Making Time Run Backward
articles.author: Michelle Starr

paras.en: Our experience of time seems uniform and unidirectional, but relativity allows it to be a bit more loosey-goosey than you might expect.
paras.zh: 我们对时间的体验似乎是统一和单向的，但相对论让它比你想象的更加松散。

paras.en: For example, in a strong gravitational field, time runs more slowly compared to time farther away – as though gravity itself were dragging it out.
paras.zh: 例如，在强引力场中，与距离较远的时间相比，时间运行得更慢——就好像引力本身将时间拖出来一样。

paras.en: Likewise, if you travel fast enough, time will pass more slowly for you compared to someone who stays behind.
paras.zh: 同样，如果你走得足够快，与留下来的人相比，你的时间会过得更慢。

paras.en: In these examples, time still only flows in one direction.
paras.zh: 在这些例子中，时间仍然只朝一个方向流动。

paras.en: But looking beyond relativity, into the realm of quantum mechanics, another possibility emerges – one in which time might not merely slow down, but effectively run backward.
paras.zh: 但超越相对论，进入量子力学领域，出现了另一种可能性——时间可能不仅会减慢，而且实际上会倒退。

paras.en: What happens when it does, though? A new mathematical exploration of this question has returned a surprising answer: The quantum environment itself imposes a limit on how far back time can effectively run.
paras.zh: 但是，当它发生时会发生什么呢？对这个问题的一项新的数学探索得出了一个令人惊讶的答案：量子环境本身对时间可以有效运行多远施加了限制。

paras.en: For the simplest model explored by physicists Yakir Aharonov of Tel Aviv University and Avshalom C. Elitzur of the Israel Institute for Advanced Research, time could only effectively run backward for about a femtosecond – or one quadrillionth of a second.
paras.zh: 对于特拉维夫大学的物理学家 Yakir Aharonov 和以色列高级研究所的 Avshalom C. Elitzur 探索的最简单模型来说，时间只能有效地向后运行约一飞秒，即万亿分之一秒。

paras.en: Their work is detailed in a preprint uploaded to arXiv.
paras.zh: 他们的工作在上传到 arXiv 的预印本中有详细介绍。

paras.en: This isn't Aharonov's first time-reversal rodeo.
paras.zh: 这并不是阿哈罗诺夫第一次进行时间逆转牛仔竞技表演。

paras.en: In 1990, he and his colleagues proposed a theoretical device called a quantum time-translation machine, which could exploit the strange properties of quantum mechanics to make a system behave as though time had sped up, stopped, or even run backward.
paras.zh: 1990年，他和他的同事提出了一种称为量子时间翻译机的理论装置，它可以利用量子力学的奇怪特性，使系统表现得好像时间加速、停止，甚至倒退。

paras.en: The idea hinges on a quirk of quantum mechanics called superposition, in which a system can exist in a combination of different possible states at once.
paras.zh: 这个想法取决于量子力学的一个怪癖，即叠加态，其中一个系统可以同时以不同可能状态的组合存在。

paras.en: Imagine you have a clock in such a state of superposition, occupying two different positions in a gravitational field at once – with enough of a difference in gravitational strength to affect the rate at which time passes.
paras.zh: 想象一下，你有一个处于这种叠加状态的时钟，它同时占据引力场中的两个不同位置——引力强度的差异足以影响时间流逝的速度。

paras.en: In one position, deeper in the gravitational field, time passes more slowly. In the other, farther away, time passes more quickly.
paras.zh: 在某一位置，引力场越深，时间流逝得越慢。另一方面，距离较远，时间过得更快。

paras.en: Quantum mechanics allows both possibilities to coexist. And when the two branches of the clock are brought back together, they can interfere with each other.
paras.zh: 量子力学允许这两种可能性共存。当时钟的两个分支重新组合在一起时，它们可能会互相干扰。

paras.en: Here's where things get weird. By selecting a particular outcome of that interference – a process called post-selection – physicists can theoretically make the clock behave as though it has experienced an amount of time outside the range of either possibility.
paras.zh: 这就是事情变得奇怪的地方。通过选择这种干扰的特定结果（称为后选择的过程），物理学家理论上可以使时钟表现得好像它经历了两种可能性范围之外的一段时间。

paras.en: That could mean more time than has passed for either branch. It could mean no time at all. Or it could mean a negative amount of time – as though the clock had been running backward.
paras.zh: 这可能意味着比这两个分支所花费的时间更长。这可能意味着根本没有时间。或者它可能意味着负数的时间——就好像时钟倒退了一样。

paras.en: Now, 36 years later, Aharonov and Elitzur have returned to the idea to investigate a particularly thorny question: How far could that negative time actually go?
paras.zh: 现在，36 年后，阿哈罗诺夫和埃利祖尔又回到了这个想法，以调查一个特别棘手的问题：那个负时间实际上能走多远？

paras.en: Because the concept remains theoretical, rather than experimentally realized, the pair turned to mathematics to explore four slightly different configurations of the machine.
paras.zh: 由于这个概念仍然是理论上的，而不是通过实验实现的，因此两人转向数学来探索机器的四种略有不同的配置。

paras.en: But before they could start, they had to answer a deceptively simple question.
paras.zh: 但在开始之前，他们必须回答一个看似简单的问题。

paras.en: Suppose you do manage to make time run backward. How in the heck do you prove it?
paras.zh: 假设你确实设法让时间倒流。你到底如何证明这一点？

paras.en: And this is where a little bit of atomic decay steals the floor.
paras.zh: 这就是一点点原子衰变的地方。

paras.en: When an atom absorbs energy, one of its electrons can jump to a higher energy level, putting the atom into what's known as an excited state.
paras.zh: 当原子吸收能量时，它的一个电子可以跃迁到更高的能级，使原子进入所谓的激发态。

paras.en: But atoms are a little bit lazy – they tend to settle back to their unexcited state (relatable). Eventually, the electron can drop back to a lower energy level, releasing the excess energy as a photon. This process is called spontaneous emission, and under ordinary circumstances, it only goes one way.
paras.zh: 但原子有点懒——它们倾向于恢复到未激发的状态（相关）。最终，电子可以回落到较低的能级，以光子的形式释放多余的能量。这一过程称为自发发射，一般情况下，它只会单向发射。

paras.en: So the researchers proposed starting with a collection of atoms that had already begun to decay, and seeing whether their theoretical machine could reverse the process.
paras.zh: 因此，研究人员建议从一组已经开始衰变的原子开始，看看他们的理论机器是否可以逆转这一过程。

paras.en: Imagine you have 100 excited atoms. You wait until some of them have released their energy, leaving just 80 still excited.
paras.zh: 想象一下你有 100 个受激发的原子。你等到他们中的一些人释放了他们的能量，只剩下 80 个人仍然兴奋。

paras.en: Now suppose you put those 100 atoms through the theoretical time machine.
paras.zh: 现在假设您将这 100 个原子放入理论时间机器中。

paras.en: If you end up with more than 80 excited atoms, the machine has effectively reversed some of the decay that had already taken place.
paras.zh: 如果最终得到超过 80 个受激原子，机器就有效地逆转了一些已经发生的衰变。

paras.en: Now, if time really did run backward, the emitted light would have to return to the atoms, restoring them to their excited states – which poses a new problem. The photons might already have traveled away, or been absorbed by something else.
paras.zh: 现在，如果时间真的倒退，发出的光必须返回原子，将它们恢复到激发态——这提出了一个新问题。光子可能已经离开，或者被其他东西吸收。

paras.en: To account for all of this, Aharonov and Elitzur imagined enclosing the atoms inside a completely sealed cell, along with the light they emitted and walls that could absorb it.
paras.zh: 为了解释这一切，阿哈罗诺夫和埃利祖尔想象将原子封闭在一个完全密封的细胞内，以及它们发出的光和可以吸收光的墙壁。

paras.en: The entire cell would then pass through the theoretical machine, allowing the researchers to investigate whether the whole process could effectively be reversed.
paras.zh: 然后整个细胞将通过理论机器，使研究人员能够研究整个过程是否可以有效地逆转。

paras.en: And here's where a rather draconian barrier emerged.
paras.zh: 这就是一个相当严厉的障碍出现的地方。

paras.en: Even inside a sealed cell, the atoms don't exist in isolation. As they emit light, they interact with the surrounding electromagnetic field, leaving traces of what has happened.
paras.zh: 即使在密封的细胞内，原子也不是孤立存在的。当它们发光时，它们与周围的电磁场相互作用，留下所发生事件的痕迹。

paras.en: For the simplest version of the machine, reversing the decay depends on those interactions retaining the quantum coherence needed for the two possible histories to interfere.
paras.zh: 对于机器的最简单版本，逆转衰变取决于那些保留两个可能的历史发生干涉所需的量子相干性的相互作用。

paras.en: But that window doesn't stay open for long.
paras.zh: 但这扇窗户不会打开太久。

paras.en: In the researchers' optical example, it lasts around one femtosecond.
paras.zh: 在研究人员的光学示例中，它持续约一飞秒。

paras.en: Beyond that, the environment has effectively retained too much information about the emission for the simplest two-branch machine to produce the desired reversal.
paras.zh: 除此之外，环境有效地保留了太多关于最简单的两分支机器的排放信息，无法产生所需的逆转。

paras.en: So the limit isn't imposed by time – it's imposed by the environment's memory of the light.
paras.zh: 所以这个限制不是由时间决定的——而是由环境对光的记忆决定的。

paras.en: More elaborate versions of the machine could theoretically reverse longer intervals, but only by introducing vastly more quantum branches, with increasingly improbable chances of success.
paras.zh: 理论上，更复杂的机器版本可以逆转更长的间隔，但只能通过引入更多的量子分支，而成功的机会也越来越小。

paras.en: But what, you are now no doubt asking, about the second law of thermodynamics? A salient point, sage reader, and one the researchers addressed directly.
paras.zh: 但是，您现在无疑会问，热力学第二定律是什么？这是一个突出的问题，明智的读者，也是研究人员直接解决的问题。

paras.en: According to the second law of thermodynamics, the total entropy of an isolated system can never decrease. Natural processes tend to move in one direction, from more ordered states to less ordered ones.
paras.zh: 根据热力学第二定律，孤立系统的总熵永远不会减少。自然过程倾向于朝一个方向移动，从更有序的状态到不太有序的状态。

paras.en: As Sir Arthur Eddington so succinctly put it, "If your theory is found to be against the Second law of thermodynamics I can give you no hope; there is nothing for it but to collapse in deepest humiliation."
paras.zh: 正如阿瑟·爱丁顿爵士简洁地说的那样：“如果你的理论被发现违反热力学第二定律，我就不能给你任何希望；除了在最深的耻辱中崩溃之外，别无他法。”

paras.en: But if time could run in reverse, wouldn't that violate the second law? Well, not necessarily.
paras.zh: 但如果时间可以倒转，那不是违背了热力学第二定律吗？嗯，不一定。

paras.en: The loophole lies in post-selection. The apparent reversal of time occurs only in a very small fraction of possible outcomes, carefully selected from all the others.
paras.zh: 漏洞在于事后选择。明显的时间逆转只发生在所有可能结果中的极小部分中，这些结果是从所有其他结果中精心挑选出来的。

paras.en: When all the outcomes are considered together, the system as a whole still obeys the second law of thermodynamics. Entropy hasn't magically started decreasing across the board.
paras.zh: 当所有结果一起考虑时，系统作为一个整体仍然遵守热力学第二定律。熵并没有神奇地开始全面减少。

paras.en: So Aharonov and Elitzur's theoretical machine can produce something that looks like time running backward without overturning one of the most fundamental laws of physics – thus evading Eddington's threatened humiliation.
paras.zh: 因此，阿哈罗诺夫和埃利祖尔的理论机器可以产生看起来像时间倒流的东西，而不会推翻最基本的物理定律之一——从而避免爱丁顿威胁要羞辱。

paras.en: But why go to such extraordinary lengths to risk an eggy face?
paras.zh: 但为什么要花这么大的力气去冒一张蛋蛋脸的风险呢？

paras.en: Well, because the question isn't really whether we can build a machine that sends things backward through time. It's why time appears to move in only one direction in the first place.
paras.zh: 好吧，因为问题实际上并不在于我们是否可以建造一台可以让事物通过时间倒退的机器。这就是为什么时间一开始似乎只朝一个方向移动。

paras.en: Many of the fundamental equations of physics work just as well backward as forward. Yet the world we experience is full of processes that seem impossible to undo.
paras.zh: 许多物理学的基本方程无论是向前还是向后都同样有效。然而，我们所经历的世界充满了似乎无法逆转的过程。

paras.en: By identifying exactly where quantum time reversal breaks down, Aharonov and Elitzur's work could help physicists understand how the environment gives rise to the irreversible processes that define our experience of time.
paras.zh: 通过准确识别量子时间反转发生故障的位置，阿哈罗诺夫和埃利祖尔的工作可以帮助物理学家了解环境如何产生定义我们时间体验的不可逆过程。

paras.en: "The arrow of time enters exactly where the machine stops," the researchers write.
paras.zh: 研究人员写道：“时间之箭正好进入机器停止的地方。”

paras.en: The research is available on preprint server arXiv.
paras.zh: 该研究可在预印本服务器 arXiv 上获取。

articles.title: Study of 26,000 Men Links Low Testosterone to 18% Higher Risk of Dying From Cancer
articles.author: Carly Cassella

paras.en: Low testosterone – popularly known as 'low T' – may have a deadly association.
paras.zh: 低睾酮——俗称“低T”——可能有致命的关联。

paras.en: A recent systematic review has found that men with very low levels of this crucial sex hormone have a higher risk of developing and dying from cancer.
paras.zh: 最近的一项系统审查发现，这种重要性激素水平极低的男性患癌症和死于癌症的风险更高。

paras.en: The research, published in the journal Lancet Healthy Longevity, analyzed long-term data from more than 26,000 men in Australia, the United States, and Europe.
paras.zh: 这项研究发表在《柳叶刀健康长寿》杂志上，分析了澳大利亚、美国和欧洲 26,000 多名男性的长期数据。

paras.en: "What we saw was that if a man had low testosterone levels – in the lowest one-fifth compared to the highest one-fifth of the range – their subsequent risk of dying from cancer was higher, even after allowing for age and other health-related factors," explains senior author and endocrinologist Bu Yeap from The University of Western Australia.
paras.zh: “我们发现，如果一个男性的睾酮水平较低——最低的五分之一与最高的五分之一相比——即使考虑到年龄和其他健康相关因素，他们随后死于癌症的风险也会更高，”资深作者、西澳大利亚大学内分泌学家 Bu Yeap 解释道。

paras.en: Specifically, men with the lowest testosterone levels had an 18 percent higher relative risk of dying from any cancer.
paras.zh: 具体来说，睾酮水平最低的男性死于任何癌症的相对风险要高出 18%。

paras.en: But testosterone was not alone. Three other hormones were also linked to cancer in the study.
paras.zh: 但睾丸激素并不孤单。研究中其他三种激素也与癌症有关。

paras.en: Men with the lowest levels of dihydrotestosterone (DHT), a potent hormone derived from testosterone, had a 21 percent higher relative risk of cancer death.
paras.zh: 双氢睾酮 (DHT)（一种源自睾酮的强效激素）水平最低的男性，其癌症死亡相对风险高出 21%。

paras.en: What's more, men with the lowest levels of sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG) had a 28 percent higher relative risk of prostate cancer, and those with the lowest levels of luteinizing hormone had a 45 percent higher risk.
paras.zh: 更重要的是，性激素结合球蛋白 (SHBG) 水平最低的男性患前列腺癌的相对风险高出 28%，而黄体生成素水平最低的男性患前列腺癌的相对风险高出 45%。

paras.en: SHBG helps carry testosterone in the bloodstream and ultimately determines how much 'free' testosterone is up for grabs.
paras.zh: SHBG 有助于在血液中携带睾酮，并最终决定有多少“游离”睾酮可供争夺。

paras.en: Luteinizing hormone, meanwhile, is produced by the pituitary gland in the brain, and it stimulates testosterone production.
paras.zh: 与此同时，黄体生成素是由大脑中的垂体产生的，它会刺激睾酮的产生。

paras.en: Interestingly, testosterone levels were not linked to prostate cancer.
paras.zh: 有趣的是，睾酮水平与前列腺癌无关。

paras.en: "Since reducing testosterone levels is a treatment for prostate cancer there's always been a question of whether the amount of testosterone your own body makes relates to your risk of prostate cancer but based on our findings there's no evidence they are related," says Yeap.
paras.zh: Yeap 说：“由于降低睾酮水平是前列腺癌的一种治疗方法，因此一直存在一个问题，即您体内产生的睾酮水平是否与患前列腺癌的风险有关，但根据我们的发现，没有证据表明它们之间存在相关性。”

paras.en: Testosterone is a crucial hormone in the male body, produced by the testes and the adrenal glands. It is involved in everything from sexual function and muscle mass to bone health and metabolism.
paras.zh: 睾酮是男性体内重要的激素，由睾丸和肾上腺产生。它涉及从性功能和肌肉质量到骨骼健康和新陈代谢的各个方面。

paras.en: But while it's completely normal for concentrations of testosterone to decrease with age, especially low levels may be a marker of poor health.
paras.zh: 虽然睾酮浓度随着年龄的增长而降低是完全正常的，但特别低的水平可能是健康状况不佳的标志。

paras.en: In the current review, when baseline testosterone was below 8.6 nmol/L, the subsequent risk of dying from cancer started increasing.
paras.zh: 在当前的审查中，当基线睾酮低于 8.6 nmol/L 时，随后死于癌症的风险开始增加。

paras.en: Today, 'low T' has become a scapegoat for practically everything that can go wrong in the male body.
paras.zh: 如今，“低 T”已成为男性身体几乎所有可能出现问题的替罪羊。

paras.en: But while low levels of this hormone are associated with numerous negative health outcomes in aging men, that does not mean testosterone is necessarily the cause, or that replacing this hormone can help.
paras.zh: 但是，虽然这种激素水平低与老年男性的许多负面健康结果有关，但这并不意味着睾丸激素一定是原因，或者替代这种激素可以有所帮助。

paras.en: Online influencers and a booming industry for testosterone replacement therapy have picked up that narrative and run far beyond the science.
paras.zh: 网络影响者和蓬勃发展的睾酮替代疗法行业已经接受了这种说法，并且远远超出了科学范围。

paras.en: In 2023, for instance, a large randomized trial followed more than 5,000 men with low testosterone for several years.
paras.zh: 例如，2023 年，一项大型随机试验对 5,000 多名睾酮水平较低的男性进行了数年跟踪。

paras.en: It found that testosterone replacement therapy did not significantly change their prostate cancer risk.
paras.zh: 研究发现，睾酮替代疗法并没有显着改变他们患前列腺癌的风险。

paras.en: "While we've shown low levels are associated with increased risk, we haven't got any evidence yet that actually giving men testosterone will reduce that risk," says Yeap.
paras.zh: 耶普说：“虽然我们已经证明低水平与风险增加有关，但我们还没有任何证据表明真正给予男性睾酮会降低这种风险。”

paras.en: Instead, Yeap explains, the findings suggest that low testosterone could be a biomarker of poor health, "so it's possible that looking at testosterone levels could help us identify men who might do poorly if they get cancer down the track."
paras.zh: 相反，叶普解释说，研究结果表明，低睾酮水平可能是健康状况不佳的一个生物标志，“因此，观察睾酮水平可能有助于我们识别那些如果患上癌症可能会表现不佳的男性。”

paras.en: Previous studies that have investigated testosterone's relationship to cancer and cancer mortality have been mixed, with some finding no association.
paras.zh: 先前调查睾酮与癌症和癌症死亡率关系的研究结果好坏参半，有些研究发现两者之间没有关联。

paras.en: But this new review relies on research that used mass spectrometry to measure hormone levels, which is more accurate.
paras.zh: 但这项新综述依赖于使用质谱法测量激素水平的研究，这种方法更为准确。

paras.en: It also considers hormones other than testosterone but that are closely associated.
paras.zh: 它还考虑了睾酮以外但密切相关的激素。

paras.en: "What we would say to men is if they are found for whatever reason to be low in testosterone, it's important to go to the doctor for a full checkup," concludes Yeap.
paras.zh: “我们要对男性说的是，如果他们因某种原因被发现睾丸激素水平较低，请务必去看医生进行全面检查，”叶普总结道。

paras.en: "It may not show any sign of testicular disease, but it might show other health issues or risk factors they need to address."
paras.zh: “它可能不会显示出任何睾丸疾病的迹象，但可能会显示出他们需要解决的其他健康问题或风险因素。”

paras.en: The research has been published in The Lancet Healthy Longevity.
paras.zh: 该研究发表在《柳叶刀健康长寿》杂志上。

articles.title: Scientists Discover a 98-Million-Year-Old Mantis With 'Leaves' on Its Abdomen, Trapped in Amber
articles.author: Jess Cockerill

paras.en: In the mid-Cretaceous, a tropical rainforest in what is now Myanmar was dripping with sticky tree resin that entombed a very peculiar praying mantis.
paras.zh: 在白垩纪中期，现在缅甸境内的一片热带雨林里滴着粘稠的树脂，里面埋藏着一只非常奇特的螳螂。

paras.en: Now, 98 million years later, this insect is the earliest clear evidence in the fossil record of praying mantises mimicking plant leaves.
paras.zh: 9800万年后的今天，这种昆虫是化石记录中最早明确的螳螂模仿植物叶子的证据。

paras.en: Its abdomen bears an uncanny resemblance to the extinct plant Selaginella grimaldii, which is also known from amber specimens found in the same region.
paras.zh: 它的腹部与已灭绝的植物卷柏（Selaginella grimaldii）有着惊人的相似之处，而在同一地区发现的琥珀标本中也发现了这种植物。

paras.en: Scientists have named the insect Folimantis hyalinala in a paper published in the journal New Phytologist.
paras.zh: 科学家在《新植物学家》杂志上发表的一篇论文中将这种昆虫命名为 Folimantis hyalinala。

paras.en: The genus name Folimantis translates literally to 'leaf mantis', while hyalinala refers to the glass-like transparency of the creature's wings.
paras.zh: 属名 Folimantis 字面意思是“叶螳螂”，而 hyalinala 指的是这种生物翅膀的玻璃般透明。

paras.en: "Though the mimicry relationship between insects and plants has evolved over at least 200 million years, reliable fossil examples of insect-plant mimicry are scarce," writes paleoentomologist Hongru Yang and colleagues.
paras.zh: 古昆虫学家杨鸿儒及其同事写道：“尽管昆虫和植物之间的拟态关系已经进化了至少 2 亿年，但昆虫与植物拟态的可靠化石例子却很少。”

paras.en: "The mimicry style of F. hyalinala with Selaginella has never been reported before, and there are no species that mimic Selaginella among modern Mantodea."
paras.zh: “以前从未报道过透明卷柏与卷柏的拟态风格，现代曼托总目中也没有模仿卷柏的物种。”

paras.en: In the modern era, there are many examples of mantises that have spent so many generations on specific plants that they've come to resemble them.
paras.zh: 在现代，有很多螳螂的例子，它们在特定的植物上花费了很多代，以至于它们变得与它们相似。

paras.en: The most impressive of these is the orchid mantis, Hymenopus coronatus, a Southeast Asian species that looks like a flower, from the pink and cream hues of its petal-like body to the way it sways its body like a flower in the wind.
paras.zh: 其中最令人印象深刻的是兰花螳螂（Hymenopus coronatus），这是一种东南亚物种，看起来像一朵花，从花瓣般的身体的粉红色和奶油色到它在风中摇曳身体的方式，就像一朵花。

paras.en: But when F. hyalinala lived, flowering plants had not yet taken over – so its body has evolved over generations to look like leaves instead.
paras.zh: 但当 F. hyalinala 生存时，开花植物尚未占据主导地位，因此它的身体经过几代人的进化，看起来像叶子。

paras.en: Every mantis that looked a little more like its host plant had a better chance of sneaking up on unsuspecting prey, while being better disguised from its own predators.
paras.zh: 每只看起来更像寄主植物的螳螂都有更好的机会偷偷接近毫无戒心的猎物，同时也能更好地伪装自己的捕食者。

paras.en: Meanwhile, the plants benefitted too, protected from herbivorous insects by their mantid inhabitants.
paras.zh: 与此同时，植物也从中受益，它们受到螳螂居民的保护，免受食草昆虫的侵害。

paras.en: Evolutionary theory says those mantises reaping the benefits of looking a little more plant-like would have had a better chance of surviving to pass on their genes to the next generation.
paras.zh: 进化论认为，那些受益于看起来更像植物的螳螂将有更好的生存机会，并将其基因传递给下一代。

paras.en: Over time, this eventually resulted in the uncanny resemblance to the leaves of Selaginella.
paras.zh: 随着时间的推移，这最终导致了与卷柏叶子惊人的相似。

paras.en: The prehistoric specimen reveals that this kind of plant mimicry has been part of the mantids' evolutionary toolkit for at least 98 million years.
paras.zh: 史前标本表明，至少 9800 万年来，这种植物拟态一直是螳螂进化工具包的一部分。

paras.en: But there's something strange about F. hyalinala.
paras.zh: 但 F. hyalinala 有一些奇怪的地方。

paras.en: Many modern mantises that have evolved to mimic plants wear foliar features all over different parts of their body.
paras.zh: 许多现代螳螂已经进化成模仿植物，身体的不同部位都有叶子特征。

paras.en: F. hyalinala has leaves on its abdomen only, which could be a hint that plant mimicry began first at the rear, with modifications to other appendages like the wings and thorax emerging later.
paras.zh: F. hyalinala 仅腹部有叶子，这可能暗示植物拟态首先从后部开始，后来出现了翅膀和胸部等其他附肢的变化。

paras.en: Praying mantises actually share an ancestor with cockroaches, which lived around 274 million years ago.
paras.zh: 螳螂实际上与蟑螂有共同的祖先，蟑螂生活在大约 2.74 亿年前。

paras.en: In recent taxonomic research, scientists suggest the first distinct mantises emerged around 185 million years ago, during the Jurassic.
paras.zh: 在最近的分类学研究中，科学家们认为，第一批独特的螳螂出现于大约 1.85 亿年前的侏罗纪时期。

paras.en: At that time, the supercontinent Gondwana was in the process of breaking up.
paras.zh: 当时，冈瓦纳超大陆正处于分裂过程中。

paras.en: This geological origin story could help explain why mantises are so widespread, diverse, and so tightly adapted to their specific environments. They've had millions of generations to hone their disguises.
paras.zh: 这个地质起源故事可以帮助解释为什么螳螂如此广泛、多样化并且如此紧密地适应其特定环境。他们已经经历了数百万代人的磨练他们的伪装。

paras.en: And they're not the only insects to have done so early in the fossil record: some cockroaches (Blattodea), grasshoppers (Orthoptera), stick insects (Phasmatodea), and members of other insect families were also evolving plant-like features around this time.
paras.zh: 它们并不是唯一在化石记录中这么早就进化出植物特征的昆虫：一些蟑螂（蜚蠊总目）、蚱蜢（直翅目）、竹节虫（竹节虫总目）和其他昆虫科的成员也在这个时期进化出类似植物的特征。

paras.en: The diagram below maps out leaf mimicry seen in fossil insects against the radiation of plant species on Earth.
paras.zh: 下图描绘了化石昆虫中观察到的叶子拟态与地球上植物物种辐射的关系。

paras.en: It offers a sense of how tightly-wound the lives of plants and insects must have been as both lineages established a growing presence on land.
paras.zh: 它让人们感受到，随着植物和昆虫在陆地上的存在不断扩大，它们的生命是多么紧密地缠绕在一起。

paras.en: Unfortunately, Kachin amber mining and trade is linked to ongoing sociopolitical turmoil in Myanmar. There are concerns that the amber trade is helping to fund what the United Nations condemns as a "genocidal crime against humanity".
paras.zh: 不幸的是，克钦琥珀开采和贸易与缅甸持续的社会政治动荡有关。有人担心琥珀贸易正在为联合国谴责的“反人类种族灭绝罪”提供资金。

paras.en: In 2015, Myanmar banned the export of fossils, but specimens embedded within amber have fallen into a legal grey area.
paras.zh: 2015年，缅甸禁止出口化石，但嵌入琥珀中的标本却陷入了法律的灰色地带。

paras.en: In 2021, the Society of Vertebrate Paleontology even called for a "hard moratorium on the publication of all fossil specimens in amber obtained from sources in Myanmar after January 2021", following a military coup.
paras.zh: 2021 年，在一场军事政变之后，古脊椎动物学会甚至呼吁“严格暂停出版 2021 年 1 月后从缅甸获得的所有琥珀化石标本”。

paras.en: The F. hyalinala mantis specimen was acquired in 2015 by a collector, Fangyuan Xia, who later that year donated it to the insect evolution lab at Capital Normal University in Beijing.
paras.zh: 透明螳螂标本由收藏家夏芳园于 2015 年获得，并于同年晚些时候将其捐赠给北京首都师范大学昆虫进化实验室。

paras.en: The research has been published in New Phytologist.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《新植物学家》杂志上。

articles.title: Forcing yourself to smile can actually make you miserable

paras.en: Forcing yourself to smile can actually make you miserable
paras.zh: 强迫自己微笑实际上会让你痛苦

paras.en: - Smiling may not always make you happier, and new research suggests that forcing yourself to smile repeatedly could actually make you feel worse. In a University of Florida study involving more than 1,100 participants, researchers discovered that while a single artificial smile can provide a small mood boost, repeatedly faking smiles can erase that benefit or even reverse it.
paras.zh: - 微笑可能并不总是让你更快乐，新的研究表明，强迫自己反复微笑实际上可能会让你感觉更糟。在佛罗里达大学一项涉及 1,100 多名参与者的研究中，研究人员发现，虽然一次人工微笑可以带来轻微的情绪提升，但反复假装微笑可能会消除这种好处，甚至逆转它。

paras.en: A smile might brighten your mood, but new research suggests that forcing yourself to smile over and over can have the opposite effect. When smiling becomes an obligation, especially one tied to financial pressure, it may actually leave people feeling less happy and more irritated.
paras.zh: 微笑可能会让你的心情变得愉快，但新的研究表明，强迫自己一遍又一遍地微笑可能会产生相反的效果。当微笑成为一种义务，尤其是与经济压力相关的义务时，它实际上可能会让人们感觉不那么快乐，更恼火。

paras.en: For years, psychologist Nicholas Coles, Ph.D., studied evidence suggesting that even an artificial smile could make someone feel a little happier. Yet those findings never quite matched his own experiences.
paras.zh: 多年来，心理学家尼古拉斯·科尔斯博士研究的证据表明，即使是人造的微笑也能让人感觉更快乐一点。然而这些发现与他自己的经历并不完全相符。

paras.en: "I used to work in customer service. I actually got written up for my inability to keep smiling at work at an unnamed theme park in Florida," laughed Coles, a professor of psychology at the University of Florida. "So I'm looking at all this evidence I had accrued so far that smiling boosts happiness and realizing it flies in the face of my own experiences in the world."
paras.zh: 佛罗里达大学心理学教授科尔斯笑着说：“我以前从事客户服务工作。实际上，我因为在佛罗里达州一个不知名的主题公园工作时无法保持微笑而受到了批评。” “所以我正在研究迄今为止我积累的所有证据，证明微笑可以提高幸福感，并意识到它与我自己在世界上的经历背道而驰。”

paras.en: That contradiction inspired Coles and his colleagues to investigate what happens when people must keep smiling, rather than simply trying it once. Their findings suggest an important distinction: A brief, intentional smile can provide a small emotional lift, but repeatedly putting on a smile under pressure can undermine happiness.
paras.zh: 这种矛盾激发了科尔斯和他的同事们去研究当人们必须保持微笑时会发生什么，而不是简单地尝试一次。他们的研究结果表明了一个重要的区别：短暂的、有意的微笑可以带来轻微的情绪提升，但在压力下反复微笑会破坏幸福感。

paras.en: Testing How Forced Smiling Affects Happiness
paras.zh: 测试强迫微笑如何影响幸福感

paras.en: To explore this difference, Coles worked with researchers Annabel Dang and Joao Francisco Goes Braga Takayanagi to design an experiment that more closely resembled the demands of customer service jobs. Their findings were published on October 1 in the Journal of Experimental Social Psychology.
paras.zh: 为了探索这种差异，Coles 与研究人员 Annabel Dang 和 Joao Francisco Goes Braga Takayanagi 合作，设计了一项更接近客户服务工作需求的实验。他们的研究结果发表在 10 月 1 日的《实验社会心理学杂志》上。

paras.en: "We tried to combine the classic way of studying it in a lab with some extra ingredients that we might see in the real world. We told participants that we would pay them less if they weren't successfully smiling," Coles said. "We also controlled the number of times they have to do it, because in customer service, every interaction is another faked smile."
paras.zh: “我们试图将在实验室研究它的经典方法与我们在现实世界中可能看到的一些额外成分结合起来。我们告诉参与者，如果他们没有成功微笑，我们会少付给他们，”科尔斯说。 “我们还控制了他们必须这样做的次数，因为在客户服务中，每一次互动都是另一个假笑。”

paras.en: The online experiment initially enrolled 1,201 people, with data from 1,174 included in the final analysis. Participants were shown images designed to produce different emotional reactions. Some depicted appealing subjects, such as kittens and flowers, while others showed disturbing situations, including theft and mistreatment of animals.
paras.zh: 在线实验最初招募了1201人，最终分析了1174人的数据。向参与者展示旨在产生不同情绪反应的图像。有些描绘了吸引人的主题，例如小猫和花朵，而另一些描绘了令人不安的情况，包括盗窃和虐待动物。

paras.en: During the experiment, participants either deliberately formed a smile or allowed their facial expressions to develop naturally. Depending on their assigned group, they completed the exercise once or repeated it 10 times.
paras.zh: 在实验过程中，参与者要么故意微笑，要么让面部表情自然发展。根据分配的小组，他们完成一次练习或重复 10 次。

paras.en: To introduce an element of pressure, researchers warned half the participants that failing to follow the smiling instructions could cost them $2 from their $6 payment. However, nobody actually lost any money, and every participant received the full amount.
paras.zh: 为了引入压力因素，研究人员警告一半的参与者，如果不遵循微笑的指示，他们可能会从 6 美元的付款中损失 2 美元。然而，实际上没有人损失任何钱，每个参与者都得到了全额。

paras.en: After completing each task, participants reported how happy they felt. The results showed that the emotional effects of smiling depended on how often people had to do it and whether they felt pressured.
paras.zh: 完成每项任务后，参与者报告了他们的快乐程度。结果表明，微笑对情绪的影响取决于人们微笑的频率以及他们是否感到压力。

paras.en: When participants viewed unpleasant images, producing a single smile gave their mood a modest boost. This benefit appeared even among those who had been warned about a possible financial penalty. However, the positive effect weakened when smiling was repeated, and it disappeared when repeated smiles were combined with the threat of losing money.
paras.zh: 当参与者看到不愉快的图像时，露出一个微笑会让他们的情绪得到一定程度的提升。这种好处甚至出现在那些被警告可能会受到经济处罚的人身上。然而，当重复微笑时，积极作用就会减弱，而当重复微笑与赔钱的威胁结合在一起时，积极作用就会消失。

paras.en: The pattern was even more revealing when people looked at pleasant pictures. Smiling just once offered little additional happiness compared with allowing their faces to respond naturally. But when participants had to smile repeatedly or felt pressure to do so, their happiness ratings actually fell below those of people who responded naturally.
paras.zh: 当人们观看令人愉悦的图片时，这种模式就更加明显。与让他们的脸自然地做出反应相比，仅仅微笑一次并不能带来额外的快乐。但当参与者不得不反复微笑或感到有压力时，他们的幸福感实际上低于那些自然反应的人。

paras.en: Further analysis revealed another unexpected consequence. In the pleasant picture conditions, forced smiling was also associated with increased irritation and anger.
paras.zh: 进一步的分析揭示了另一个意想不到的结果。在令人愉快的图片条件下，强迫微笑也与增加的恼怒和愤怒有关。

paras.en: "If you only force a smile once without any financial penalties, you can see the improvement in happiness. So what psychologists were seeing in their lab is right," he said. "But when you make it a little bit more like the real world, where you have to keep repeating it, and if you don't do it well, you get financial penalties, you see it completely reverse."
paras.zh: “如果你只强颜欢笑一次而不受到任何经济处罚，你就能看到幸福感的提高。所以心理学家在实验室中看到的结果是正确的，”他说。 “但是当你让它变得更像现实世界时，你必须不断重复它，如果你做得不好，你会受到经济处罚，你会看到它完全相反。”

paras.en: The Hidden Emotional Cost of Smiling at Work
paras.zh: 工作中微笑的隐藏情感成本

paras.en: These findings may help explain why expectations to appear cheerful throughout the workday can become frustrating rather than uplifting.
paras.zh: 这些发现可能有助于解释为什么在整个工作日表现得愉快的期望会变得令人沮丧而不是令人振奋。

paras.en: The issue has already sparked controversy in the workplace. In recent years, Target faced widespread criticism over a policy requiring employees to smile when customers came within a specified distance. Although the policy was intended to encourage friendly interactions, Coles argues that such requirements can interfere with people's ability to express their emotions naturally.
paras.zh: 这个问题已经在职场上引发争议。近年来，塔吉特公司因一项要求员工在顾客进入特定距离时微笑的政策而受到广泛批评。尽管该政策的目的是鼓励友好互动，但科尔斯认为，这样的要求可能会干扰人们自然表达情绪的能力。

paras.en: The problem may extend beyond employees. Customers can also feel obligated to respond positively to friendliness that is being imposed rather than offered spontaneously. According to Coles, these expectations limit the emotional freedom of both sides of the interaction.
paras.zh: 问题可能不仅仅限于员工。顾客也会觉得有义务对强加的而不是自发提供的友好做出积极回应。科尔斯表示，这些期望限制了互动双方的情感自由。

paras.en: Could Trying Less to Be Happy Make Us Happier?
paras.zh: 少尝试快乐能让我们更快乐吗？

paras.en: After spending years investigating how people can improve their emotional well-being, Coles has begun considering a broader question. Rather than constantly searching for ways to increase happiness, might people be better off placing greater value on simply being content?
paras.zh: 在花了数年时间研究人们如何改善情绪健康后，科尔斯开始考虑一个更广泛的问题。人们不应该不断地寻找增加幸福感的方法，而更重视单纯的满足感是否会更好？

paras.en: His research suggests that efforts to manufacture positive emotions do not always produce the intended results. Sometimes, trying too hard to appear happy can make the experience less pleasant.
paras.zh: 他的研究表明，制造积极情绪的努力并不总是能产生预期的结果。有时，过于努力地表现出快乐可能会让体验变得不那么愉快。

paras.en: "As a society, we have placed such an immense amount of emphasis on trying to make ourselves feel happier than we currently are," he said, "much less emphasis on just being content with what we have."
paras.zh: 他说：“作为一个社会，我们非常重视让自己感觉比现在更幸福，更不用说满足于我们所拥有的了。”

paras.en: Materials provided by University of Florida. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由佛罗里达大学提供。注意：内容的风格和长度可能会被编辑。

paras.en: - Nicholas A. Coles, Annabel V. Dang, Joao Francisco Goes Braga Takayanagi. Smiling your way to happiness or misery? Experimental tests of competing perspectives [Registered Report - stage II]. Journal of Experimental Social Psychology, 2027; 128: 105011 DOI: 10.1016/j.jesp.2026.105011
paras.zh: - Nicholas A. Coles、Annabel V. Dang、Joao Francisco Goes Braga Takayanagi。微笑通往幸福还是痛苦？竞争观点的实验测试[注册报告 - 第二阶段]。实验社会心理学杂志，2027； 128：105011 DOI：10.1016/j.jesp.2026.105011

articles.title: 5,000-year-old skulls reveal a disturbing secret of ancient Egypt's first kings

paras.en: 5,000-year-old skulls reveal a disturbing secret of ancient Egypt's first kings
paras.zh: 5000年前的头骨揭示了古埃及第一批国王的令人不安的秘密

paras.en: - A 5,000-year-old mystery surrounding the tombs of Egyptâs first kings has taken a disturbing turn. Scientists reexamining 46 ancient skulls discovered evidence of potentially fatal head injuries in 18, suggesting that at least 39% of those studied may have been deliberately killed. The findings support a century-old theory that royal attendants were sacrificed when kings died, possibly to serve them in the afterlife.
paras.zh: - 围绕埃及第一代国王陵墓的一个长达 5000 年之久的谜团发生了令人不安的转变。科学家重新检查了 46 个古代头骨，发现其中 18 个头骨可能致命，这表明至少 39% 的研究对象可能是被故意杀害的。这些发现支持了一个已有百年历史的理论，即国王去世时，皇家侍从会被牺牲，可能是为了在来世为他们服务。

paras.en: New forensic evidence suggests that some of ancient Egypt's earliest rulers had members of their royal households killed when they died, possibly so those individuals could continue serving them in the afterlife. The discovery sheds new light on a disturbing burial practice that archaeologists suspected more than a century ago but could not prove.
paras.zh: 新的法医证据表明，一些古埃及最早的统治者死后杀死了他们的王室成员，可能是为了让这些人在来世继续为他们服务。这一发现为考古学家在一个多世纪前就怀疑但无法证实的令人不安的埋葬习俗提供了新的线索。

paras.en: The evidence comes from ancient skulls recovered near royal tombs at Abydos, Egypt, where members of the First Dynasty were buried roughly 5,000 years ago. When archaeologist Flinders Petrie excavated the graves in the 1920s, he noticed that unusually large numbers of people had been buried around the kings. He suspected that these individuals had been sacrificed following their rulers' deaths, but he could not identify physical evidence of fatal injuries.
paras.zh: 证据来自在埃及阿拜多斯皇家陵墓附近发现的古代头骨，大约 5000 年前第一王朝的成员就埋葬在那里。当考古学家 Flinders Petrie 在 20 年代挖掘坟墓时，他注意到国王周围埋葬着异常多的人。他怀疑这些人是在统治者死后被牺牲的，但他无法识别致命伤的物证。

paras.en: Now, a modern forensic examination has uncovered signs of potentially deadly head trauma in 18 of 46 skulls, representing approximately 39% of the individuals studied. The findings provide compelling new support for the theory that human sacrifice played a role in the burial traditions of ancient Egypt's first kings.
paras.zh: 现在，现代法医检查在 46 个头骨中的 18 个中发现了可能致命的头部外伤的迹象，约占研究对象的 39%。这些发现为活人祭祀在古埃及第一代国王的埋葬传统中发挥作用的理论提供了令人信服的新支持。

paras.en: "I was drawn to these retainers partly because, even though they were buried around royalty, they are mostly relegated to footnotes in the grander narrative," said Dr. Roselyn Campbell of Purdue University, who led the research published in Frontiers in Environmental Archaeology. Campbell is also the author of the forthcoming book State-sanctioned Violence and Human Sacrifice in Early Dynastic Egypt (Routledge Press).
paras.zh: 普渡大学的罗塞琳·坎贝尔博士领导了这项发表在《环境考古学前沿》上的研究，她说：“我之所以被这些家臣所吸引，部分原因是，尽管他们埋葬在皇室周围，但在宏大的叙事中，他们大多被降级为脚注。”坎贝尔还是即将出版的《埃及早期王朝的国家批准的暴力和人类牺牲》一书的作者（劳特利奇出版社）。

paras.en: "Who were these people and how did they view the ruler and their own role in his or her life and death?"
paras.zh: “这些人是谁？他们如何看待统治者以及他们自己在他或她的生死中所扮演的角色？”

paras.en: A 5,000-Year-Old Mystery Surrounding Egypt's First Kings
paras.zh: 围绕埃及第一代国王的 5000 年前的谜团

paras.en: Around 3000 BCE, the earliest kings of a unified Egypt constructed elaborate burial complexes at Abydos. These sites included royal tombs, additional burial chambers, and enclosed areas believed to have been used for funeral ceremonies.
paras.zh: 公元前 3000 年左右，统一埃及的最早国王在阿拜多斯建造了精致的墓葬群。这些遗址包括皇家陵墓、额外的墓室以及据信用于葬礼的封闭区域。

paras.en: Surrounding the main structures were numerous smaller graves arranged in rows. Some royal burial sites were accompanied by hundreds of these subsidiary burials, raising questions about why so many people had been buried in close association with a single ruler.
paras.zh: 主要建筑的周围是许多成排排列的较小坟墓。一些皇家墓地还伴随着数百座附属墓葬，这引发了人们的疑问：为什么这么多人被埋葬在与同一个统治者密切相关的地方。

paras.en: "Each subsidiary burial was a simple chamber in a row of dozens of others," said Campbell. "Some people had a simple coffin. Most people had a few grave goods, like ceramic vessels, and many graves also included small objects like copper tools, projectile points, or small ivory figurines. Petrie found a few grave markers that had names and sometimes official titles on them. The titles seem to mostly refer to lower- or mid-level officials as well as artisans."
paras.zh: 坎贝尔说：“每个附属墓葬都是一排简单的墓室，有数十个其他墓室。” “有些人有一个简单的棺材。大多数人有一些陪葬品，比如陶瓷器皿，许多坟墓还包括一些小物品，比如铜工具、弹头或小象牙雕像。皮特里发现了一些墓碑，上面有名字，有时还有官方头衔。这些头衔似乎主要指的是中低级官员和工匠。”

paras.en: The extraordinary concentration of graves led Petrie to propose that the people buried alongside the kings were victims of a practice known as retainer sacrifice.
paras.zh: 坟墓的异常集中使得皮特里提出，与国王一起埋葬的人是一种被称为家臣祭祀的做法的受害者。

paras.en: "Retainer sacrifice is a type of human sacrifice where those close to a ruler are killed when the ruler dies," explained Campbell. "In many cultures, retainer sacrifice is practiced because of beliefs that the sacrificed individuals will continue to serve the ruler in some kind of afterlife, but retainer sacrifice can also be a visceral display of the ruler's power. Some retainers might have volunteered to die to achieve eternal life or honor, others may have been chosen or even forced."
paras.zh: 坎贝尔解释说：“家臣祭祀是活人祭祀的一种，当统治者去世时，那些与统治者关系密切的人都会被杀死。” “在许多文化中，进行家臣祭祀是因为人们相信牺牲的人在来世将继续为统治者服务，但家臣祭祀也可以是统治者权力的发自内心的展示。一些家臣可能自愿死去以获得永生或荣誉，其他人可能是被选择甚至被迫的。”
