articles.title: Does A Stop-Start Engine Demand Better Oil?
articles.author: Greg Jones

paras.en: Stop-start technology is designed to improve fuel efficiency and reduce emissions, but it also alters how engines operate, especially regarding lubrication.

Each time the engine shuts off and restarts, engine oil must quickly reach critical components like the valvetrain, camshafts and upper engine areas. These repeated cycles can increase wear if the oil does not respond quickly enough.
That’s why choosing the right oil, particularly a high-quality full synthetic, plays an important role in protecting performance and supporting long-term engine life.

Stop-start systems increase the frequency of engine restarts during everyday driving, particularly in traffic. Each restart requires oil to reestablish a protective layer across key components quickly.

While no unique oil category is required, performance characteristics become more important. Oils that circulate efficiently and maintain protection under repeated cycling are better suited for these engines. Full-synthetic oils are designed to deliver that level of consistency, helping reduce the impact of frequent restarts and reducing stress on components that drive the start-stop systems.

Vehicle manufacturer recommendations should always guide oil selection. For added protection, full-synthetic motor oils are well-suited to stop-start conditions due to their ability to withstand repeated stress.
High-quality synthetic oils are engineered to circulate efficiently during startup, protect critical components under frequent cycling, and maintain stability under varying temperatures.
These properties help ensure consistent lubrication throughout drives that involve frequent stopping and starting.

Stop-start operation increases the frequency of engine transitions from off to on, introducing more frequent periods when components rely on immediate lubrication. The upper engine, including cams and valvetrain components, can be especially sensitive during these transitions. Without fast and effective oil coverage, these areas may experience increased friction over time.

Premium synthetic oils are formulated to address this by maintaining strong film strength and resisting breakdown, even under repeated cycling. Conventional oil can meet basic requirements, but it is generally less effective in managing the demands of frequent engine cycling.
Synthetic oils are more stable and adaptable across changing conditions. This allows them to maintain consistent viscosity and protection, even as the engine repeatedly cools and restarts.
In stop-start environments, where conditions change rapidly, this consistency provides a measurable advantage in maintaining protection.
However, frequent stop-and-go driving may be categorized as severe service due to possible added strain placed on engine systems and fluids.

Shops should follow manufacturer-recommended oil change intervals; and check customers’ oil life monitoring systems when available. These factors can affect how quickly oil degrades, Even with high-quality formulations, oil can degrade more or less quickly depending on driving habits and other factors.

articles.title: Concept Tire Helps VW Set EV Efficiency World Record
articles.author: Christian Hinton

paras.en: A Continental concept tire contributed to three world records set by Volkswagen‘s Mission Efficiency electric concept vehicle during a long-distance drive.

The vehicle consumed 7.51 kilowatt-hours (kWh) of electricity per 100 kilometers (approx. 60 miles), including charging losses, and 6.89 kWh excluding charging losses. RID – Rekord-Institut für Deutschland certified the record on Aug. 24.

The Mission Efficiency traveled 1,278.36 kilometers (approx. 790 miles) from Wolfsburg to Vienna under real-world conditions. The journey required one charging stop, and the vehicle finished with 164 kilometers (approx. 100 miles) of remaining range.

Continental’s specially developed tire achieved a rolling resistance of 4.9 kilograms per metric ton. That figure is approximately 25% below the threshold for the EU tire label’s highest class A rating.
According to Continental, approximately 20% of an electric vehicle’s propulsion energy goes toward overcoming tire rolling resistance. Reducing that resistance can help increase driving range.

“The record shows that increasing the range of electric cars does not necessarily require larger batteries. Significant opportunities lie in the successful interaction of all vehicle components. Tyres make a crucial contribution,” said Dr. Christian Strübel, Continental’s expert in rolling resistance for passenger car tires. “Together with Volkswagen, we’ve demonstrated what’s possible when vehicle, aerodynamics and tyre development are aligned from the very beginning.”
Continental Concept Tire Reduces Rolling Resistance
Tire rolling resistance directly affects electric vehicle energy consumption and driving range.

As a tire rotates, it deforms where it contacts the road surface. This deformation consumes energy that would otherwise be available for propulsion. Lower rolling resistance allows a vehicle to travel farther using the same battery charge.

Continental said it based its concept tire on the EcoContact 7, a production tire designed for low rolling resistance. The company modified the tire to meet Volkswagen’s specifications for the record attempt.
The resulting design reduces tire deformation during operation, helping lower energy consumption and increase range per battery charge.
Tire Construction and Manufacturing Process

Continental said it focused on two components to reduce rolling resistance: the sidewall design and tread compound. The concept tire uses the same sidewall design principle as the production EcoContact 7. This provides stability without increasing rolling resistance.
Continental said it also tailored the tread compound to work with the tire’s other components. Together with the carcass and tread pattern, the compound helps minimize energy losses during rotation.
The manufacturing process provides another opportunity to reduce rolling resistance.
During vulcanization, manufacturers use heat and pressure to harden the initially soft green tire in a mold. Conventional production typically heats the tire uniformly.

For the concept tire, Continental said it applied different temperatures to individual tire areas. The tread and sidewall undergo different curing conditions, allowing engineers to optimize their properties separately.
For the tread, this process contributes to lower rolling resistance.

Continental also said it designed the concept tire to minimize rolling noise. Engineers varied the spacing and angles of the tread blocks to create sounds that partially overlap and cancel each other.

The principle is similar to noise-canceling headphones and helps reduce the tire noise experienced inside the vehicle. This is particularly relevant for electric vehicles, where tire noise becomes more noticeable without an internal combustion engine.
Continental and Volkswagen Collaborate on Tire Development
Volkswagen’s Mission Efficiency concept is based on the ID. Polo, which uses Continental’s EcoContact 7 as standard equipment.
For the record project, Continental said it worked with Volkswagen’s vehicle and aerodynamics engineers from an early development stage.
The teams coordinated tire, vehicle and aerodynamic development to improve overall efficiency.
The collaboration also included visual design. Continental incorporated color accents and styling elements from the Mission Efficiency concept into the tire’s sidewall.
Volkswagen Mission Efficiency Sets Three Records
The Mission Efficiency established three records during its long-distance drive:
- Aerodynamics: Most aerodynamic near-production vehicle, with a drag coefficient (Cd) of 0.158.
- Energy efficiency: Most efficient four-seat electric vehicle in its class during a single drive under controlled conditions.
- Long-distance efficiency: Most economical near-production four-seat electric vehicle on an officially documented long-distance drive under real-world conditions.
The vehicle featured an aerodynamically optimized shape and additional solutions to improve airflow.
Volkswagen based the Mission Efficiency on production components from the ID. Polo, including its battery and drivetrain.
The record drive demonstrated efficiency improvements through targeted changes to existing electric vehicle technologies under real-world, long-distance driving conditions.

articles.title: TrakMotive Earns Global TÜV Certification
articles.author: Alex Crissey

paras.en: TrakMotive announced that its global CV axle product range has achieved TÜV certification.
The certification covers more than 9,700 CV axle SKUs across Europe, the United States and Mexico. The certified range includes:
- More than 3,700 SKUs for the United States

TÜV certification is recognized globally as an independent verification of product quality, testing, and manufacturing processes. TÜV-certified products are widely used across industries including automotive, electronics, industrial equipment, and medical devices.

TÜV conducted extensive product validation and manufacturing audits to confirm compliance with established quality and performance standards. The certification also includes ongoing annual surveillance audits and periodic product testing to maintain compliance.

“This certification represents a significant milestone for our global CV Axle program,” said Robert Zhu, TrakMotive’s Global CEO. “Achieving TÜV certification across such a broad product range demonstrates our long-term commitment to delivering dependable, high-quality products to customers worldwide.”

TrakMotive says it plans to incorporate the TÜV certification mark and QR verification system across various customer touchpoints, including catalogs, digital platforms, packaging, labels, and select product markings, in accordance with TÜV usage guidelines.

articles.title: The Downside of Regenerative Braking
articles.author: Joe Keene

paras.en: Regenerative braking allows electric vehicles to recover energy during deceleration. Instead of converting all vehicle momentum into heat at the brake rotors, the electric motor acts as a generator. This slows the vehicle while returning some energy to the battery.
The process can significantly reduce the use of conventional friction brakes. However, reduced brake usage can also create maintenance challenges involving corrosion and component operation.
On conventional internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles, brake pads regularly contact the rotors during braking. This friction helps remove light surface corrosion from the rotor faces.
EVs with aggressive regenerative braking may use their friction brakes less frequently. Exposure to moisture, road salt and humidity can then allow corrosion to develop on the rotor surfaces.
EV Regenerative Braking and Rotor Corrosion
Light surface rust is not necessarily a problem because normal brake applications can remove it. However, corrosion can progress when friction brakes are not used regularly.
Over time, heavier rust, pitting and scaling can develop on the rotors. Once the rotor surfaces deteriorate significantly, normal brake applications may not restore their condition.
Reduced friction brake usage can also extend brake pad life. However, brake components can develop problems unrelated to friction material wear.

Corrosion may form around brake pad hardware, caliper brackets, slide pins and other components. Pads can become restricted in their brackets, while caliper components may develop problems from limited movement.
As a result, brake components may require replacement because of corrosion or restricted movement rather than normal wear.
How Regenerative and Friction Braking Work Together
Electric vehicles still require conventional hydraulic friction brakes to maintain stopping performance.

Regenerative braking may become reduced or unavailable under certain operating conditions. These include a fully charged battery, very cold battery temperatures, vehicle stability control intervention or certain system faults.
EV braking systems blend regenerative braking with conventional hydraulic friction braking to provide the stopping performance drivers expect.
This makes conventional brake system condition an important consideration, even when regenerative braking reduces normal friction brake usage.
EV Brake Inspection and Maintenance Considerations
Technicians should account for reduced friction brake usage when inspecting electric vehicle braking systems.
Measuring brake pad thickness alone may not provide a complete picture of component condition.

EV regenerative braking improves efficiency by recovering energy and can substantially extend brake pad life. However, reduced friction brake usage can also increase the potential for corrosion and restricted component movement.
Brake condition assessments should account for both friction material wear and the effects of limited brake usage.

articles.title: The AAM Group Announces 2026 Keys to Ride Winner
articles.author: Jeff White

Johnny joined five other finalists for the final drawing Nov. 5 at the Lippert booth during the SEMA Show. He won a 2025 Ram 2500 featuring customizations from the Lippert family of brands.
The AAM Group Recognizes Sweepstakes Finalists

articles.title: Career Driver’s AI Agent Helps Drivers Connect With Carriers
articles.author: Kevin Linger

paras.en: Career Driver and Truck Drivers USA expanded their recruiting partnership with a new driver agent that can contact carriers, schedule conversations, and help drivers move through the hiring process.
The Career Driver driver agent is available through the Career Driver mobile app and is designed to act on a driver’s behalf rather than simply return job listings or answer questions.
The companies describe it as the first driver agent of its kind in transportation.

“Our partnership with Career Driver started with a shared vision for creating a better mobile experience for drivers, but we’ve always seen the opportunity to build something much bigger together,” said Lori Furnell, president of Truck Drivers USA.
Drivers can use the agent to identify job opportunities and take the next step toward connecting with an employer.

The Career Driver driver agent can call carriers, coordinate conversations, and schedule calls based on the jobs a driver is interested in. The companies said the goal is to reduce the amount of searching, calling, and coordination drivers must handle themselves.
For carriers, the system creates another recruiting touchpoint. Recruiting teams can communicate with a driver’s agent to coordinate calls with interested candidates.
Carriers can also have job openings featured in the Career Driver app through Truck Drivers USA.
Read the full article on fleetequipmentmag.com.

articles.title: ATRI Elects Ben McLean Board Chairman, Adds Two Members
articles.author: Kevin Linger

paras.en: The American Transportation Research Institute (ATRI) elected Ben McLean as ATRI board chairman. He will lead the research organization’s 13-member board.
The institute also appointed Ben Banks, president of TCW, and Nathan Meisgeier, president and chief legal officer of Werner Enterprises.
McLean, CEO of Ruan Transportation Management Systems, succeeds Derek Leathers, chairman and CEO of Werner Enterprises. Leathers is completing four years as ATRI chair.

“We are excited to have Ben McLean lead the ATRI Board,” said Rebecca Brewster, ATRI president and COO. “His commitment to research excellence and innovation will help drive the Institute forward for years to come. We also want to thank Derek Leathers for his dedicated service as Chairman and welcome Ben Banks and Nathan Meisgeier to the Board. Their extensive industry experience and insights will be tremendous assets to ATRI as we continue advancing our research mission.”
Board Members Bring Research and Fleet Leadership Experience

The new ATRI board chairman joined the board in October 2017. McLean has served as Ruan’s CEO since 2015, after joining the carrier in 2007. His previous positions included chief operating officer and chief information officer.

Banks has worked at TCW for more than 15 years. He previously served as a member and chair of ATRI’s Research Advisory Committee and is a 2018 graduate of the American Trucking Associations’ LEAD program.

Meisgeier has served as Werner’s president and chief legal officer since January 2024 and also serves as chief of staff. He joined the company in 2005, and his responsibilities include legal, safety, risk, human resources, recruiting, and government affairs.
He also chairs the American Trucking Associations’ Legal Reform Advisory Committee and serves on its Litigation Center board.

articles.title: Dorman Products Introduces Aluminum Oil Filter Housing
articles.author: Jeff White

paras.en: Dorman Products Inc. continues expanding its aftermarket product offerings with repair solutions that address common failure points in original equipment parts. The company recently launched a new OE FIX engine oil filter housing (part number 926-611) for select Genesis, Hyundai and Kia vehicles.

“Dorman continues to launch new innovations that expand the breadth of our product offerings and provide customers with improved solutions to common original equipment problems,” said Eric Luftig, Dorman’s President, Light Duty. “Our OE FIX products are designed to give technicians greater confidence that a repair will be completed right the first time, with a more durable solution that helps reduce the risk of repeat failures and costly comebacks. By continuing to identify common failure points and develop better repair solutions, we create new opportunities for our customers while helping them deliver greater value to the technicians and vehicle owners they serve.”

paras.en: Dorman Addresses Common Oil Filter Housing Failures

The original equipment oil filter housing on certain Genesis, Hyundai and Kia vehicles uses plastic that can warp. Prolonged exposure to heat and chemicals under the hood can cause the plastic to degrade. Over time, the housing can leak oil or crack.
Replacing the failed part with another original equipment housing can leave the vehicle vulnerable to the same failure.

Dorman manufactures the 926-611 OE FIX replacement from high-pressure die-cast aluminum for a more durable repair. The housing includes the required mounting gaskets, premium seals, an oil filter element and an oil filter cap. These components provide technicians with everything needed for a complete installation.
Dorman engineered the product in the United States to precise specifications that help resist future leaks and provide reliable service.
Company Expands Oil Filter Housing Portfolio
The 926-611 builds on the performance of Dorman’s patented 926-959 aluminum oil filter housing. That product serves a wide range of Chrysler, Dodge, Jeep, Ram and Volkswagen vehicles.
Launched in 2023, the 926-959 has become one of the company’s most successful offerings.

Dorman has expanded its portfolio of oil filter housings, adapters, coolers, assemblies and seals. The product line addresses common original equipment failure points and aims to help technicians avoid repeat repairs.
The new engine oil filter housing is among the Dorman OE FIX solutions featured in the company’s sixth OE FIX Guide. It joins the thousands of OE FIX solutions Dorman currently offers.
The guide highlights products with improved designs, time-saving features and cost-efficient repair options.

articles.title: NAPA Opens First Highly Automated Reverse Logistics Center
articles.author: Mary DellaValle

paras.en: NAPA recently celebrated the grand opening of its York Reverse Logistics Center (RLC), marking the debut of the first highly automated facility of its kind within the NAPA network and an important milestone in the company’s ongoing supply chain transformation.

The 400,000-square-foot center combines more than 100 robots and advanced automation technology with a skilled local workforce to process returns, cores and inventory for redistribution across the NAPA Northeast distribution network.

The center began operations earlier this year and is designed to accelerate returns processing, helping get parts back into inventory faster and improving availability for NAPA stores, repair professionals and their customers, the company said. The new facility, which can support 250,000 unique SKUs, is expected to reduce the time needed to prepare inventory for redistribution by 43% and support inventory accuracy up to 99.5%.

Leaders from NAPA and corporate parent Genuine Parts Company (GPC) were joined by York Mayor Sandie Walker, state and local elected officials, the York County Economic Alliance, community partners and teammates for a ribbon-cutting ceremony and tours of the facility at 500 Willow Springs Lane.

“York is the first step in a broader modernization of the NAPA supply chain,” said Justin Ducharme, executive vice president, supply chain, NAPA. “By combining innovative technology with the expertise of our teammates, we’re creating a more efficient operation that helps keep parts moving to the customers and repair professionals who rely on us every day.”

During the ceremony, the GPC Foundation presented a $2,500 Good Neighbor grant to United Way of York County. The grant supports the foundation’s mobility priority and reflects a shared belief that reliable transportation opens access to jobs, health care and stronger family life.

As the first highly automated reverse logistics center within the NAPA network, RLC represents an important milestone in the company’s efforts to enhance operational capabilities and support the growing needs of customers across the Northeast, the company said.

articles.title: Advance Auto Parts Opens First Store in King of Prussia
articles.author: Mary DellaValle

paras.en: Advance Auto Parts opened its first store in King of Prussia, Pennsylvania, expanding access to parts, tools and expertise for local drivers and automotive professionals. The company marked the opening of the store at 125 W. Dekalb Pike with a ribbon-cutting ceremony alongside local officials and representatives from Central Montco Technical High School who were on site to accept a donation for the school’s automotive technology program.

The donation will help students gain hands-on experience, training and career opportunities through the school’s automotive technology programs. Skilled automotive technicians continue to be in high demand, with approximately 70,000 openings projected annually through 2034, according to U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics.

“We’re excited to bring Advance Auto Parts to King of Prussia and open our first store in the community,” said Eli Rosa, regional vice president, Advance Auto Parts. “In addition to serving local customers, this market hub will help strengthen support for professional technicians and nearby shops across the area. We’re proud to mark the occasion by supporting Central Montco Technical High School and the programs that help students prepare for automotive technician careers.”

“We appreciate Advance Auto Parts’ support of career and technical education,” said Craig Robinson, administrative director at Central Montco Technical High School. “This donation helps support the hands-on learning experiences that are at the core of our automotive technology program and gives students opportunities to build skills they’ll use long after graduation.”

The new store also serves as a market hub – a centralized facility designed to improve parts availability and same-day fulfillment across a network of stores, enhancing hard parts coverage for professional customers, Advance Auto Parts said.

articles.title: Romans carefully dismantled statue of emperor when they withdrew from Scotland 1,800 years ago, leaving only his foot behind
articles.author: Kristina Killgrove

paras.en: All that remains of a larger-than-life statue of the Roman emperor Antoninus Pius once erected in Scotland is a lower right leg. Experts have now reconstructed what the entire sculpture looked like but are still unsure why it was carefully dismantled over 1,800 years ago.

The gold-covered bronze foot and calf, also known as the Milsington leg, was discovered in a bog in 1820, according to a Nov. 12 statement from National Museums Scotland. It is the only example of a monumental Roman emperor statue ever found in Scotland and was likely made around A.D. 140.

Initially, experts thought the bronze statue had been looted from York, England, which was founded by the Romans in A.D. 71 as the town of Eboracum. But as research into the Roman frontier advanced over the years, it became clear that equestrian statues were often set up in forts along the border of the Roman Empire.
This lower leg, experts now believe, originally came from an equestrian statue of Emperor Antoninus Pius that was similar to the famous statue of Marcus Aurelius in Rome.

Antoninus Pius was Roman emperor from A.D. 138 to 161, succeeding Hadrian, who had built an enormous wall to defend the northernmost limit of the Roman Empire. To add to Rome's territory, Antoninus Pius directed the imperial governor of Roman Britain to move north, invade southern Scotland and build a second wall, called the Antonine Wall. But that wall was left undefended after Antoninus Pius died, and the Romans retreated from Scotland.

During that retreat, the Romans may have dismantled any valuable statues that they had set up, according to the statement. An examination of the Milsington leg ahead of a new exhibition showed that the bronze had no cut marks, suggesting it was removed carefully and not "brutally hacked off."

"This contrasts with examples of statues being deliberately destroyed after a battle, when an emperor's memory was condemned, or when they were chopped up for scrap," according to National Museums Scotland.
Get the world’s most fascinating discoveries delivered straight to your inbox.
With the Scottish provenance firmly established, National Museums Scotland curators were able to learn more about Antoninus Pius and his approach to imperial expansion.

"This really turns on its head our understanding of Rome's second attempt at conquering Scotland," Fraser Hunter, principal curator of prehistoric art and Roman archaeology at National Museums Scotland, said in the statement. "This was a big deal for the Emperor, something which was worth celebrating."

But while the boot-clad bronze leg provides a glimpse into the monuments that may have graced southern Scotland nearly two millennia ago, it raises an important question for Hunter: Where is the rest of the statue?

The Milsington leg, the Inveresk Mithras altars and other Roman-period finds are on display beginning Nov. 14 in the exhibit "Roman Scotland: Life on the Edge of Empire" at the National Museum of Scotland.
From Augustus to Nero, see how much you know about ancient Rome's famous leaders with our Roman emperor quiz!

Kristina Killgrove is a staff writer at Live Science with a focus on archaeology and paleoanthropology news. Her articles have also appeared in venues such as Forbes, Smithsonian, and Mental Floss. Kristina holds a Ph.D. in biological anthropology and an M.A. in classical archaeology from the University of North Carolina, as well as a B.A. in Latin from the University of Virginia, and she was formerly a university professor and researcher. She has received awards from the Society for American Archaeology and the American Anthropological Association for her science writing.

articles.title: 'Godless' founder of utilitarianism had severe dental problems and was in 'excruciating pain,' CT scans of his severed head reveal
articles.author: Tom Metcalfe

paras.en: The great and "godless" English philosopher Jeremy Bentham, whose remains have been on display at a U.K. university for over 150 years, suffered from severe dental problems, according to X-ray scans of his skull.

The scans were conducted with CT (computed tomography) scanning equipment to create a digital 3D model of his head and highlight Bentham's lengthy "presence" at University College London (UCL) as it celebrates its 200th anniversary.

The scans revealed that Bentham was missing many teeth and had advanced arthritis in his lower jaw when he died of natural causes at the age of 84. During the scanning process, project leader Tannis Davidson, curator of UCL's Grant Museum of Zoology, saw how thin the jawbone had become. "He must have been in excruciating pain," she told Live Science.

Bentham's utilitarian philosophy inspired UCL's founders; it was only the third university in England, after Oxford and Cambridge, which was founded as London University in 1826 and opened to students in 1828.

As a young man, Bentham had declared that he would donate his body to science after his death. This was a radical idea at the time; in the U.K., dissection after death was looked down upon, even if it was for scientific purposes, and it was reserved for the worst criminals. After Bentham died in 1832, his remains were fashioned into an auto-icon — a supposed replica of himself — to memorialize him in the way a tombstone might, Davidson said.
Except for brief visits across Europe and to the Met Breuer in New York City, this auto-icon has been in a display case at UCL since the 1850s, where it can be seen by students as they pass by.

To make the auto-icon (which is not a mummy), Bentham's body was dissected and studied. Then, his skeleton was dressed in his clothes, which were padded with straw. His severed head was badly disfigured during an attempt to preserve it with sulfuric acid, so a wax reconstruction based on paintings and death masks was attached to the body.
Get the world’s most fascinating discoveries delivered straight to your inbox.

Bentham's real head was displayed at the feet of the clothed skeleton that had a lifelike wax head; the real head's eyes were replaced with highly detailed glass eyes, which can be seen in the scans. According to UCL lore, the real head was stolen in 1975 and held ransom for a few days by rivals from King's College London, after which it was locked away.

Davidson explained that Bentham had coined the term "auto-icon" to mean "self-representation" and was setting an example for others. "He imagined a future where people were making auto-icons to keep their dead relatives around," she said.

The CT scans of the real head show that Bentham had dental damage and jaw arthritis, and that his brain had been removed before it was preserved—although some of his dura mater, a layer of connective tissue that covers the brain and spinal cord, was preserved. Davidson said the brain extraction was done to keep with Bentham's instructions that his head be mummified in the same way as Māori heads, which had their brains removed. The scanning process is shown in a short film called "Bentham Revealed."
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Bentham wrote about his dental problems several times, Davidson said, but it is not clear if he understood that he also had severe arthritis in his lower jaw, which must have made the problems with his teeth much more painful. In addition, modern ideas about cleaning teeth had not been established by Bentham's time. "Dentistry 200 years ago was a very different kettle of fish than it is today," Davidson said.

Bentham was a polymath who hoped to improve the lives of ordinary people through social reform. He wrote extensively about subjects as varied as law, economics, education and animal rights, and he believed that society could be engineered to produce better outcomes through legislation and the objective measurement of "utility."

His most famous idea was the panopticon in 1791, a ring-shaped prison with one warden to watch all of the prisoners, which he proposed as a humane alternative to Australia's penal colonies. Today, however, it is a symbol of state control and surveillance. Bentham also invented a "felicific calculus" to numerically assess the benefits and drawbacks of any given action, based on variables like its intensity, duration, certainty, purity and extent.
Bentham's philosophy put him at odds with the established Church of England; he called himself an "unbeliever," while critics called him "godless."

This rift with the church may have played a part in Bentham's wishes for his remains. Davidson suggested that the auto-icon may have been a means for Bentham to avoid being buried with traditional Anglican rites. "Maybe this was a way he could 'stick it to them' a little bit," she said.

Tom Metcalfe is a freelance journalist and regular Live Science contributor who is based in London in the United Kingdom. Tom writes mainly about science, space, archaeology, the Earth and the oceans. He has also written for the BBC, NBC News, National Geographic, Scientific American, Air & Space, and many others.

articles.title: Scientists discover two adorable species of howler monkey in the Amazon — and they're already endangered
articles.author: Sascha Pare

paras.en: Scientists have identified two newfound species of howler monkey in the Amazon rainforest. The discoveries could redraw branches of these primates' evolutionary tree, a new study shows.

The new species were named Alouatta iroi and Alouatta matogrossensis. The adorable creatures have bushy beards, winsome expressions and bright red fur. Their identification raises the number of known howler monkey species to 16, researchers said in a statement.

"Our study shows that the Amazon still holds remarkable biological secrets, even among well-known animals such as howler monkeys," study first author Romina Batista, a biodiversity scientist at the University of Gothenburg in Sweden and the University of Salford in the U.K., said in the statement.
One of the newfound species, A. matogrossensis, is probably on the brink of extinction. The other newfound species faces threats from a planned dam on the Rio Branco River, according to the study.

In addition to identifying the new species, the study, published Oct. 30 in the journal Communications Biology, used genetic evidence to understand when howler monkeys spread out and diversified. The researchers analyzed the genomes of 11 howler monkey species living in South and Central America, combining existing DNA datasets with new genomic information from specimens in Brazilian zoological collections.
Overall, the genetic data confirmed that howler monkeys diverged from close relatives between 19 million and 13.5 million years ago. But the analysis changed the picture of more recent evolution.

For instance, the team argued that the Tapajós red-handed howler (A. tapajozensis) and the Amazonian black howler (A. nigerrima) are not as closely related as scientists previously thought. The researchers also said that the Trinidad howler (A. insulanus), whose status has been unclear, should be confirmed as a separate species.
Get the world’s most fascinating discoveries delivered straight to your inbox.

"This discovery comes at a critical time, as increasing deforestation, climate change and habitat loss threaten many Amazonian species before they are fully understood or even discovered by science," study co-author Jean Boubli, a professor and chair of primate ecology and evolution at the University of Salford in the U.K., said in the statement.

The scientists found that natural barriers such as the Amazon River, the Xingu River and the Branco River drove many howler monkeys to develop separately. Researchers believe that howler monkeys can swim across small waterways, but big rivers block groups from mixing, which led to different traits and species evolving over time. Natural barriers are a common reason why species emerge in the Amazon, the researchers noted in the study.

articles.title: This Four-Person NASA Crew Spent Over a Year on 'Mars.' Here's What They Did for 378 Days in a Simulated Martian Habitat

paras.en: On October 31, four NASA crewmembers returned from “Mars.” Not the actual Red Planet, of course, but a 3D-printed Mars habitat in Houston where the three men and one woman lived for 378 days.

Now, the Mars analog astronauts—Ross Elder, Ellen Ellis, James Spicer and Matthew Montgomery—have started telling the world what took place after they disappeared into NASA’s Mars Dune Alpha habitat at the Johnson Space Center on October 19, 2025, for the agency’s second Crew Health and Performance Exploration Analog (CHAPEA) mission.

The mission aimed to test the kinds of physical and mental conditions that a team of Mars explorers would endure on the Red Planet, including long-term isolation, disrupted communication with people on Earth and food cultivation. The habitat includes both a base and a mock outdoor environment, so the crew could practice Marswalks.

“For more than a year, they have lived in an isolated environment, conducting critical research and helping us better understand what it will take to send humans to Mars,” Vanessa Wyche, director of NASA’s Johnson Space Center, said during a livestream, just before the crew emerged. “Inside just 1,700 square feet, they managed to live with limited resources. They maintained their habitat. They grew crops, and they carried out simulated Mars operations.”

After the speech, NASA astronaut Jack Hathaway, who had just completed a mission at the International Space Station, knocked on the door to the Mars habitat, called out “trick or treat” and opened it to reveal the crew’s smiling faces. Since then, the analog astronauts have been participating in post-mission evaluations and debriefs that, along with the data collected during their year in the simulated environment, will help inform future missions to Mars and those closer to home, per a NASA statement.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: “Most days, we had things that were scheduled, from maintenance and science and engineering activities and some operational activities. So, we often do extravehicular activities, also known as EVAs or spacewalks,” Elder, who was the mission’s commander and test pilot, tells CNN News Central. “We would do drone and rover operations where we control certain equipment outside of the habitat, and we would practice additional data collection for both human health and behavioral sciences.”

Each team member brought unique expertise to the mission. Elder was an experimental test pilot at the U.S. Air Force. Ellis, the mission’s medical officer and tactical thinker, is a U.S. Space Force officer. Spicer was the flight engineer and systems specialist, and he has experience in satellite communications and spacecraft development. Montgomery’s diverse background in hardware engineering, robotics, technology startups and independent films made him the “Swiss Army knife of crewmates;” he served as the mission’s science officer and versatile engineer.

paras.en: Quick fact: When was the first CHAPEA mission?

The first mission of this kind also lasted 378 days, during which crewmembers Kelly Haston, Ross Brockwell, Nathan Jones and Anca Selariu entered the Mars Dune Alpha habitat on June 25, 2023, and emerged on July 6, 2024.

Elder tells Fox News that combining their skills created “magic.” But that didn’t happen by accident; the selection process lasted about a year and a half and included personality evaluations by NASA psychologists, Montgomery tells the outlet. What’s more, they got to practice before entering the habitat.

“The crew spent a lot of time together prior to the mission, so we got to work on our teamwork and build relationships,” Montgomery tells Nature’s Kaia Glickman, including during a winter camping expedition that overlapped with a blizzard. “These high-pressure scenarios set a nice foundation for pre-training, where we spent five weeks together before going into isolation. Through all of those tools that we built, we had a really good dynamic as a team inside of the habitat, and conflict was very minimal.”

paras.en: Montgomery and his crewmates could still speak with mission control, but the communication system intentionally mimicked delays that would occur on a real Mars mission. That meant messages could take up to 22 minutes to deliver, and the team even had to deal with a planned two-week communication blackout. Future travelers to Mars will experience this communications barrier when Earth and the Red Planet are temporarily on opposite sides of the sun, blocking radio signals from traveling between the planets, according to Nature.

articles.title: Archaeologists in England Discovered 8,000 Roman-Era Frog Bones in a Single Ditch. They Just Solved the Mystery of How the Amphibians Ended Up There

paras.en: Between 2016 and 2022, archaeologists conducting excavations along a planned stretch of England’s A14 highway unearthed an array of astonishing discoveries, including a Roman amulet carved to resemble the mythical Gorgon Medusa, the earliest physical evidence of beer production in Britain and an Iron Age comb crafted from a human skull.

Comprising more than 280,000 artifacts, the finds—uncovered between modern-day Cambridge and Huntingdon—shed light on life in the region over roughly 12,000 years. But some discoveries raised more questions than answers: Why, for example, did a single ditch at the Bar Hill site in rural Cambridgeshire contain some 8,000 amphibian bones?

As Vicki Ewens, a senior zooarchaeologist at the Museum of London Archaeology (MOLA), told the Observer’s Dalya Alberge in 2022, “In my experience, mainly working on sites from London, we don’t get that many frogs. To have so many bones coming from one ditch is extraordinary.”

Ewens and her colleagues outlined several possible explanations for the unusual cache. Perhaps the amphibians fell into the ditch (also described as a gully) and found themselves trapped. Or maybe they succumbed to extreme cold during their wintertime hibernation. Alternatively, they could have served as the centerpiece of a meal—or several—enjoyed by Iron Age humans, although the absence of cut marks on the bones rendered this scenario unlikely.

Four years after MOLA first announced the find, experts have finally solved the mystery of the ancient animal cemetery. Based on a groundbreaking analysis of amphibian arm bones, researchers led by Ewens and Paul Clarkson, an archaeologist at England’s Bournemouth University, concluded that most of the frogs whose remains were found in the ditch died young, eaten by birds of prey such as short-eared owls and hen harriers in the second or third century C.E., during Britain’s Roman era.

A combination of environmental factors and human activity produced ideal conditions for this avian feast to unfold over a relatively short timeframe. As the authors write in the journal Environmental Archaeology, water levels in the Fens—the marshy wetland that houses the gully—retreated during the Roman period, enabling frogs in drying-out ponds to reproduce at a faster rate. When birds in search of their next meal arrived, they had no trouble spotting their prey: Locals had felled the trees in the area to make way for grazing livestock, leaving the amphibians with limited woodland protection from aerial predators.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: - All toads are frogs, but not all frogs are toads. Both animals belong to the Anura order, meaning they are amphibians that lack tails.

- According to the University of Michigan’s Animal Diversity Web database, “There is no scientific distinction between ‘frogs’ and ‘toads,’ although most anurans are usually referred to as one or the other.”

“We don’t often get an owl’s eye view of what it was like in the past from archaeological sites,” Clarkson says in a statement. “These bones not only tell us about life for people living near the Roman Fens, but they also give insights into the natural world—what wild animals were getting up to in the past, and what life was like for them.”

The majority of the bones belonged to frogs and toads (specifically common frogs), but shrews, voles and mice were also present in the assemblage. The remains represented no fewer than 469 individual animals.

To estimate the frogs’ ages at their time of death, the researchers measured the amphibians’ distal humeri, or arm bones—a method previously described by Clarkson and several co-authors in a 2025 paper. According to the study, the team determined that a large number of the frogs died in either their first or second year of life, during a “short, intensive predation event” spanning autumn to the following spring, “probably along migration routes to and from hibernation sites.” An abundance of frogs likely attracted “local and migrant predators to the area to feed on them and also, coincidentally, on other locally available prey, such as voles, insectivores, birds and fish.”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Based on breakage patterns and physical traces of digestion seen on the bones, the paper’s authors ruled out several species that typically prey on amphibians, including otters, gray herons and grass snakes. Instead, they suggest that the “lightly digested and relatively unbroken bones” are more consistent with medium-sized birds such as short-eared owls.

Initially, the archaeologists identified the gully as a roundhouse in an enclosure dating to Britain’s Iron Age, which began around 750 B.C.E. and ended with the Roman invasion in 43 C.E. But radiocarbon dating of the bones shifted this timeline forward by several hundred years.

How did humans fit into this puzzle? Although the researchers considered the possibility that ancient people intentionally deposited the bones in the ditch, the only evidence for this scenario was the presence of a Roman-era brooch among the animal remains. In all likelihood, the authors argue in the paper, the mass predation event only took place because humans weren’t in the area at the time: Short-eared owls “only choose quiet roosting sites, so people must have rarely visited this area, particularly with dogs.”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Why locals steered clear of this specific spot in the autumn and winter remains unclear, but the scientists posit that “the most probable explanation is seasonal movement of livestock.” Avoidance tied to social or ritual reasons is also possible.

“I had so many theories as to why such [a] large collection of frog bones were recovered from this small feature,” Ewens says in the statement. “This research shows how even the smallest animal recovered on a site can help us to understand not only past environmental conditions but human activity within a wider landscape.”

articles.title: Thawing Permafrost May Have Created a New Type of Landslide, Which Could Become More Common as the World Warms

paras.en: In 2017 and 2018, a pair of strange landslides moved huge masses of rock and dirt in Canada’s Northwest Territories. The events occurred in the central Mackenzie Valley, and one of them even dammed a river and created a lake.

The two natural disasters are part of a new class of landslides scientists are calling “permafrost detachment slides” in a study published in the journal Geophysical Research Letters in September. They may have been partially triggered by severe wildfires that occurred in 1995, which destabilized the ground and allowed the base of the permafrost to thaw. What’s more, these events may become more common as the planet continues to warm.

“It’s a very dramatic manifestation of the changing climate,” says study co-author Joseph Young, a geoscientist who conducted the work at the University of Alberta in Canada, to Matt Simon at Grist. “They’ve only started happening in the last 10, 15 years, and it’s a very drastic and abrupt change in the landscape.”

Young and his colleagues began the study after seeing something strange in the Northwest Territories in 2019. While conducting field research, they spotted large landslide scars in valleys that they knew were stable permafrost, or permanently frozen earth, reports Stephanie Pappas for Live Science.

To better understand what happened, the team homed in on two major events: the Johnson River slide in August 2017 that moved about 4.5 million cubic meters of dirt and rock, and the Redstone River slide in August 2018 that sent roughly 18 million cubic meters of debris tumbling down. Satellite imagery captured between 1980 and 2020 and field studies revealed some odd characteristics, the team found.

“Typically with permafrost, everything just thaws and melts in a slurry and moves like a mud downslope,” Young tells Live Science. “But with these large landslides, we found blocks of frozen material in the debris.”

The team monitored the temperature near the 1995 burn area near the slides and, for comparison, undisturbed forest from September 2020 to August 2022. Their data went into computer simulations, which allowed the researchers to investigate how the wildfires decades earlier may have affected the region.

Their resulting hypothesis? The fires that swept through the landscape burned off the vegetation that usually keeps the permafrost cool on sunny days. “After about 20 years or so, that thermal signature from the burned forest can reach the base of permafrost,” Young tells Grist. “It’s slight, but it’s there.”

As the frozen ground warmed, it weakened and formed cracks, allowing water to seep in. That allowed the permafrost to thaw even more, destabilizing its bottom layers. Eventually, that caused the ground to detach and created the two landslides at the center of the study. They’re among more than 150 permafrost landslides in the area that happened around two decades after the severe wildfires, meaning the newly proposed mechanism could have contributed to many of these catastrophic events.

The findings suggest scientists need to better study what’s happening below the surface of permafrost regions, says Dmitry Nicolsky, a geophysicist at the University of Alaska Fairbanks who wasn’t involved in the work, to Nikk Ogasa at Science News. “We don’t know how [the ground] will move—it might go slowly or it might go catastrophically.”
Thankfully, Young says experts can look out for signs of an impending permafrost detachment slide and predict when it’s going to happen.

“That’s kind of the silver lining,” he tells Julia Parrish at the CBC. “It doesn’t just happen overnight; it kind of happens in a more progressive manner over the course of about 20 years after a fire, where you get a slow downslope movement of these slopes.”

articles.title: Microsoft 365 Crawls Back to Life After a 24-Hour Outage
articles.author: Andrew Couts

paras.en: Sorry, Margaret, your email is working again.

After a widespread outage shut down Microsoft 365 services for businesses, governments, and tens of millions of other users around the world, the essential cloud services are now (mostly) back online, according to the company’s status page.

The outage debacle began around lunchtime on the East Coast on Thursday, with users reporting Outlook outages to the service-tracking website Downdetector just after 12 pm ET. Within the hour, Microsoft said it was investigating reports of an outage that at the time was limited to North America. It quickly spread to impact more than 70 countries around the world.

The full cause of Microsoft’s unprecedented outage remains unknown, but the company repeatedly ruled out a cyberattack as the cause in statements to its status page. It is also ruling out AI or AI agents playing a role in the debacle.

“We are seeing broad recovery and stability across our services,” a Microsoft spokesperson says in a statement. “This was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI/agents. The incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change. We have addressed the underlying issue and continue to restore service to remaining customers and regions.”
The company has promised a “full post-incident report” after it has fully reviewed what went wrong.

As Outlook, Teams, Copilot, and other Microsoft 365 systems come back online, users will likely see their inboxes turn into a mess. “You're probably going to get a lot of notifications when things come back,” says Jonathan Leitschuh, an independent researcher.

Microsoft said it had increased the queue time for emails to 48 hours in an attempt to ensure that every message that people tried to send while its systems were down gets delivered. Leitschuh points out that, even with the bulk of systems restored, users may receive “a flood of notifications a few hours down the pike” as subsystems come back online.

The total impact of the Microsoft outage may never be fully known, but it’s safe to say it’s already significant. Governments from Japan to the United States reported disruptions to a bevy of functions. Airlines reported problems with their ability to communicate with customers. Many law enforcement and emergency services ground to a halt. And hospitals reported widespread interruptions to their operations.

Ultimately, the episode serves as a reminder of the risks involved when the whole world relies on a single company for a critical service. “We're very interdependent on these systems in modern life,” says Leitschuh. Next time, delayed emails may be the least of our worries.

articles.title: Taylor Swift couldn't write 'Toy Story 5' song 'until I was in my 30s'

paras.en: LOS ANGELES, Nov. 13 (UPI) -- Taylor Swift said her song from Toy Story 5, "I Knew It, I Knew You," reflected maturity she's come to in her own life. The song plays at the end of the film and is on the soundtrack.
In Toy Story 5Joan Cusack) visits the home where her former owner, Emily, grew up. A new family, with a young daughter Blaze (Mykal-Michelle Harris), lives there now.

In a recent Zoom press conference with the Critics Choice Association, Swift, 36, described her process of writing the song with Jack Antonoff. She responded to the way the film gave Jessie closure over her heartbreak from 1999's Toy Story 2.

"I was so struck by the lessons that Jessie learned," Swift said. "I think that resonated with me because they were lessons I learned in my life. Maybe I wouldn't be able to write this song until I was in my 30s. It takes a long time to process and perceive memory with acceptance."
Without spoiling Jessie's discovery for viewers yet to watch the latest film, which is now on home video, she finds clues to Emily's life without her.

"This specific type of gratitude that this song is about, it just feels like it's something I've arrived at more recently in my life," Swift said. "I don't think I was ready to write about it in this type of way until I saw Jessie experience it."

In Toy Story 2, Woody the cowboy (Tom Hanks) met Jessie when he discovered he was part of a collectible Woody's Roundup set. Jessie told him the story of Emily outgrowing her and donating her to charity.
Jessie has remained a part of Woody's gang through the Toy Story sequels. Only in Toy Story 5 does she find some evidence that Emily did not just forget about her toy. Swift could relate.

"There's a weight lifted because you realize you don't have to carry that particular thing around anymore," she said. "It took me a while to realize how to release certain things from the load you drag around. I happened to see the movie at the perfect time to write this."
As much as she related to Jessie, Swift also felt relief writing a song in her character. Many of Swift's own songs are autobiographical.

"In another way there is a pressure release valve of not having to write about my personal life," Swift said. "Being able to absorb myself in a story that I wasn't just watching unfold when I watched Toy Story 5, I've been watching this story unfold since I was 5."

The original Toy Story came out in November 1995. Toy Story 2 was 1999. Sarah McLachlan sang "When She Loved Me" about Jessie remembering Emily's childhood, and longing for the days when she loved her.

"That song is so perfect and devastating that there are times that I will just think about it and feel like I'm gonna cry," Swift said. "I don't even need to hear it to feel that way. It's so potent and it's so powerful. It's really sorrow and heartbreak and grief in its purest form."

Swift's song was able to offer healing to Jessie, and viewers who have remained devastated by Toy Story 2 since the last century. Jessie cannot go back to being Emily's toy, but she learns she made a positive impact on Emily's adult life.
"You can be there for someone for a time in their lives and make an impact and that can be enough to really mean something," Swift said. "I wanted to hint at 'When She Loved Me' and then heal it."
Randy Newman has been the composer and songwriter for the entire Toy Story franchise. His original song "You've Got a Friend In Me" has been the theme for the whole series.

So Swift and Antonoff wanted to honor Newman and compose a song that fit with his franchise aesthetics. Swift described how that stretched her musically with chord progressions she would not typically write for herself.

"It's on that line of 'Life has ways of leaving those days behind,' I would have gone for an A minor," Swift said. "Instead we go to an A7 and then resolve in a D minor. It almost feels like you're about to modulate but you don't."
Swift also incorporated instruments she would not normally orchestrate, such a virginal harpsichord.

"We've got tenor sax, we've got baritone sax and they're playing in a way that is structured in a different way than we would normally do it," Swift said. "We would normally have very structured parts. Whereas in our world of trying to reach towards Randy Newman, we felt it could feel more like a jam band with individual players acting as characters."
Swift did want "I Knew It, I Knew You" to sound like country music, to go with Jessie.
"I think that her time on Woody's Roundup and her being a cowgirl, I know how to bring that in," Swift said. "We've got banjo, we've got mandolin, harmonica."

The musical arrangement came after the lyrics, Swift said. Lyrically, Swift said she wanted the words to have a double meaning, allegorically and literally. She explained the opening line as an example, "I knew you through the daze of the blades of the grass in summer."

"As an allegory, it's youth," she said. "It's the people who knew you when you didn't wear shoes very often. You were always outside, you were always covered in dirt, you were always sunburnt. That's a very specific version of you for someone to know."
Literally, the line describes the point of view of toys.
"When they're standing on the ground looking up at their kid, they're looking through the blades of grass because they're toys," she said

articles.title: Memo: White House staff must get approval to meet with lobbyists

paras.en: Nov. 13 (UPI) -- White House staff are no longer allowed to meet with lobbyists without prior approval, according to a memo by Chief of Staff Stephen Miller.
The memo, which was first obtained by Politico, went out Thursday night and says that staffers must get approval from the Office of White House Counsel before meeting with a lobbyist.

"No President in history has fought more relentlessly, selflessly or courageously for the American People than President Trump. Following his example, White House staff are expected to dedicate their time unwaveringly to the working people of the nation," the memo said.
Miller replaced former White House Chief of Staff Suzie Wiles after she was ousted three days after the midterm elections.
Miller isn't friendly with lobbyists, Politico said.

"The thing with Stephen [Miller] is, he's not someone that a lobbyist goes in and has to crack or try to win over," said Hunter Morgen, a lobbyist at Ballard Partners who worked with Miller during the first Trump administration. "He doesn't operate based on relationships. He operates based on policy outcomes that will advance the president's agenda."
A dozen lobbyists told Politico that Miller doesn't take relationship-based favors and isn't influenced on issues. He's driven by ideology and fiercely loyal to President Donald Trump, they said.

"Even in his deputy chief of staff role, he cared enough to be at Rose Garden dinners and Christmas parties and events that the donor community was invited to, like they do in all administrations," a Republican lobbyist who attends social events at White House, told Politico. "So it's not like he's an alien to that scene ... it's just going to be done differently."

"He's impossible to lobby, no one can do it, not even the people that you would think are closest," one of the lobbyists said. "I think he's more reasonable than he's being portrayed, but he's not swayed by lobbying."

articles.title: Arizona Cardinals sign tight end Elijah Higgins to 3-year extension

paras.en: Nov. 13 (UPI) -- The Arizona Cardinals signed tight end Elijah Higgins to a three-year extension, they announced Friday.
Higgins' agency, Equity Sports, said the pact is worth up to $26.8 million. The fourth-year tight end was entering the final season of his rookie contract.

Higgins, 26, was a sixth-round pick by the Miami Dolphins in the 2023 NFL Draft. The former collegiate wide receiver was waived by the Dolphins and claimed off waivers by the Cardinals in August of 2023.
Higgins caught 18 passes for 162 yards and a score through nine appearances this season. He hauled in 82 passes for 798 yards and four scores through his first four seasons for the Cardinals.
Higgins totaled career-highs in catches (30) and receiving yards (301) last season, when he appeared in 17 games for the Cardinals.
The Cardinals (3-6) will host the Los Angeles Rams (5-4) at 4:05 p.m. EST Sunday in Glendale, Ariz.

articles.title: Eisenkot Accuses Netanyahu of Fueling ‘Racist’ Hostility Against Arabs
articles.author: Adam Rasgon

paras.en: Gadi Eisenkot, the former military chief who is trying to form the next Israeli government, accused Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Friday of fueling a “racist” campaign against the country’s Arab citizens, in some of the strongest public criticism of his rival’s attacks on the community.

The comments were made days after Mr. Netanyahu delivered a divisive speech to the opening session of Parliament, or the Knesset, in which he referred to Arab lawmakers as “terror supporters” and “haters of Israel.” Diplomats and analysts condemned the remarks as a brazen display of hatred and incitement against Arab citizens, who make up about 20 percent of the overall population, and voted in massive numbers in inconclusive elections last month.

“Since the beginning of the election campaign, they have been subjected to a racist and aggressive campaign of delegitimization, fueled by the outgoing prime minister and those around him for political purposes,” Mr. Eisenkot said in a statement on social media.
“Arab citizens of Israel are an integral part of the Israeli story,” he said, adding that it was wrong to malign an entire community.

“The attempt to marginalize them and vilify them collectively is a profound violation of the principles of statesmanship,” Mr. Eisenkot said. “It dishonors Israel’s Declaration of Independence and the values we take pride in as a Jewish and democratic state.”
The Declaration of Independence says all citizens have equal social and political rights “irrespective of religion, race or sex.”

articles.title: Europe Agrees on a Team to Represent It in Talks With Russia
articles.author: Jeanna Smialek

paras.en: European leaders have waited on the margins of negotiations to end Russia’s war in Ukraine for months, eyeing a seat at the table. They learned this week that they would get one, and simply needed to decide which official should sit in that chair.

European Union leaders concluded in Dublin on Friday that they will tap a group of major nations — Britain, France, Germany, Poland, and Italy — along with a representative from the E.U’s leadership arms, the European Council and European Commission.

In some ways, the choice of a crowd plays into jibes Americans have made about the continent’s indecisiveness: “If Europe could identify one person to speak on their behalf, that would be a bigger achievement than getting the Russians to include them in the negotiation,” Jared Kushner, President Trump’s son-in-law and a U.S. envoy, said earlier this week.

Europe’s failure to pick one negotiator leaves open the possibility that its fragmentation will diminish its influence. Even so, Europeans have underscored that they are a democracy of many nations, though, and that many voices must be represented.
“We decide on who represents us, and that is what we have done today,” said Ursula von der Leyen, the president of the European Commission.
“We need to work as a team,” António Costa, president of the European Union’s political leadership arm, said at a news conference on Friday, noting that America itself has two envoys.

articles.title: Microsoft’s Global Outage and Fixes: What We Know
articles.author: Michael Levenson

paras.en: Microsoft is reporting widespread improvements to its services after a global outage took them offline on Thursday, disrupting communications and work at schools, government agencies and offices around the world. The company, headquartered in Redmond, Wash., said on Friday that it was seeing “encouraging recovery progress, with service availability and email delivery performance improving across a growing portion of affected infrastructure.”
“We remain focused on addressing residual impact and ensuring reliable service restoration,” the company added.
Here’s what to know as of Friday afternoon.

Outages started disrupting Microsoft tools and apps around noon Eastern time on Thursday and quickly spread to more than 70 countries and territories, affecting millions of users, according to Downdetector, an outage-tracking site.
Some of Microsoft’s most popular products, including the email manager Outlook, the workplace messaging and video calling app Teams and the artificial intelligence assistant Copilot, stopped working.

Microsoft said in a statement on Friday that “for now, we can confirm that there is no indication this is the result of malicious or cyber activity.” It added that the problem was “a technical issue not related to cyber or A.I.” agents.
So why were Microsoft’s systems not working?
The company has yet to provide a clear answer, although it has promised to make public a full report that identifies the “root cause” of the outage.

articles.title: Gene Autry’s Guitar in Global Dispute
articles.author: Jessica Nicholson

paras.en: As programmers prepare Christmas playlists, the Gene Autry recordings “Rudolph, the Red-Nosed Reindeer” and “Here Comes Santa Claus (Down Santa Claus Lane)” are currently top of mind.

But a 1931 Autry recording – “That Silver-Haired Daddy of Mine,” which charted on Billboard’s all-genre hit parade in 1935 – is suddenly timely, as well, in a real-life detective story that’s erupted into a trans-Atlantic legal tiff.

A rare Martin OM-45 guitar, one of only 50 produced in the early-1930s, was found in a Swedish farmhouse among the inheritance a father left to his daughter when he died in February 2021. The guitar, it turns out, was likely owned by Autry and stolen from him in 1932. The exact journey the instrument took cannot be fully traced, but steps were taken somewhere in the past 90 years to conceal its identity. The process of uncovering the guitar’s authenticity and tracing its original ownership back to Autry, a Country Music Hall of Fame member who was an iconic singing cowboy during much of the 20th century, reads like a C.S.I. forensics drama, laid out in a four-part series by Swedish newspaper Göteborgs-Posten.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Autry’s widow, Jackie Autry, is now embroiled in a tug of war over the instrument, which she believes should be returned to the Autry Museum of the American West, a Los Angeles institution that documents cowboy and Native American history.
“I don’t have any of Gene’s guitars anymore,” Jackie told Göteborgs-Posten. “They’re all at the museum now because that’s where it belongs. It belongs to the public, not to me, not to her.”
“Her” would be the daughter of Owe Jakobsson, a Swedish woman named Sandra who was left in charge of her daddy’s estate after his death.

Owe had inherited the instrument from his father, Gunnar, who was an inventive repairman. The original guitar had amateur-grade modifications made to the neck and bridge, and Sandra received a $7,000 offer for the Martin when she was selling off pieces of the estate. Another potential buyer tipped her off that it was likely worth far more, and they discovered that even a modern replica is worth about $12,000. This guitar, which had all the earmarks of being an original, could be worth six figures.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Sandra took the instrument to a Stockholm guitar shop for restoration, and there, Leif Lundbäck discovered a name, Gene Autry, that had been covered with black paint. He also found a serial number when he detached the neck. The Martin company, they would discover, has documentation from several letters that Gene wrote in early 1932 that verify a connection.
The singer’s 1932 tax return, produced by the estate, indicates that a Martin guitar had been stolen from him in the fall, roughly nine months after his correspondence with Martin.

Autry’s widow, Jackie, offered $20,000 for the instrument after she was contacted. Sandra declined that figure, holding that the guitar has sentimental value because she had inherited it from her father. The two sides are at a stalemate – Autry has not increased her offer and told Göteborgs-Posten, “I don’t pay money to blackmailers.”

Sandra has been advised that the guitar is worth far more, and that Autry’s estate can afford it. The case is complicated by differing nuances in the laws of Sweden and the United States. “I’m the one who inherited it,” Sandra told Göteborgs-Posten. “So, with that said, I don’t think I’m being dishonest by wanting to keep it.
Go here to read the full, four-part series.

articles.title: Latin Grammys 2026 Recap: Rosalía & Karol G Win, Daddy Yankee Is Honored & More | Billboard News
articles.author: Katie Cao

paras.en: From Rosalía’s wins for album of the year (Lux) and song of the year (“La Perla”) to Karol G’s best urban music album victory for Tropicoqueta, we’re looking back at the the 2026 Latin Grammy’s biggest wins, emotional speeches and standout performances. Watch Daddy Yankee’s person of the year tribute, Juanes and Carín León’s duet, and the moving José Alfredo Jiménez tribute featuring The Warning and Camila Fernández.

Narrator: Legendary moments, unexpected surprises and amazing performances. We’re in Las Vegas, and Billboard, together with Lexus, celebrate the magic of the Latin Grammys with a recap of everything you missed, presented by Lexus.

Karol G wins best urban music album for Tropicoqueta. Rosalía swept the top prize for song of the year for her catchy “La Perla” and crowned the night by conquering the coveted trophy for album of the year for Lux. Milo J took home the award for record of the year for “Niño.” Xavi wins his first Latin Grammy and dedicates it to Mexico. Also, newcomer Aria Vega won the coveted award for best new artist.

But let’s not forget these moments. Rosalía premiered the performance among the clouds of Lux alongside a dance cast of celestial aesthetics. And Daddy Yankee, named person of the year, got everyone on their feet singing along with a medley of his greatest hits that featured the participation of a star-studded cast: J Wheeler, French Montana, Feid, Punjabi artist Diljit Dosanjh and even LL Cool J. Could this be a preview of what Daddy Yankee has in store?

articles.title: Eminem Joins IDK for Hard-Hitting J Dilla-Produced ‘Welcome’ as DMV Rapper Signs to Shady Records
articles.author: Michael Saponara

paras.en: With IDK joining the Shady Records roster, Eminem teamed up with the DMV-bred rapper for the fittingly titled new single “Welcome” on Friday (Nov. 13). The song also features production from the late, great Detroit beatmaker J Dilla.

Dilla sets the tone with his signature thumping drums and a menacing beat, which Em catches for a sinister chorus. “Welcome to the party where everybody dies at the end/ Move your body/ This is ’bout to be a homicide scene/ I think you are not mean when I scream,” he raps.

Slim Shady didn’t put a verse on “Welcome,” as it appears he wanted IDK to fully shine. The 34-year-old makes the most of his moment next to Em, showing off his dexterity as a rhymer. “We run this s–t, y’all n—as walk/ That’s why she twerkin’ all that a– when she take it off/ You— you know we talk that slick talk, that slick talk,” IDK raps while shrewdly sneaking in an interpolation of Future’s 2016 hit “Stick Talk.”
A black-and-white visual accompanied the release, which finds Eminem making an appearance alongside IDK. They take turns rapping in an apartment building hallway before IDK hits the town.

It’s a new era for IDK, who signed to Shady Records in partnership with Interscope Records. Hype for a possible Eminem collab surged earlier this week when the duo posed for a photo together in the studio on social media.

“When I first started working on this music, I remember looking up at my ceiling and saying, ‘Thank you’. I was speaking to Dilla because it felt like everything that could have been, in a way, started to clear itself organically,” IDK said in a statement. “I knew this was an important opportunity and a statement for hip-hop itself.”

He continued: “The first rap album I’ve ever owned was 50 Cent’s Get Rich or Die Tryin’. A Shady Records release. The first raps I made it a point to memorize were Eminem raps. I’ve been at it for some time now, so to be at the point in my journey seems surreal. I’m excited for this next chapter in my career.”

IDK released his e.t.d.s. (Even the Devil Smiles) project in January, which featured appearances from hip-hop heavyweights such as RZA, Pusha T, the late DMX and MF DOOM as well as Black Thought and No ID.

articles.title: When Kevin Feige Got Off to a Less-Than-Incredible Start at Marvel
articles.author: Lexy Perez

paras.en: The success that Marvel Studios honcho Kevin Feige has achieved over the two-plus decades since landing on The Hollywood Reporter‘s Next Gen list in 2003 would likely make any producer green with envy.

Boston-born and New Jersey-raised, Feige was rejected from USC film school five times before finally getting accepted. He later landed an unpaid internship with Superman director Richard Donner and his wife, producer Lauren Shuler Donner. Feige continued working as an assistant for Shuler Donner, leading him to earn an associate producer credit for Fox’s 2000 release X-Men. Feige’s passion for the company impressed Marvel Studios founder Avi Arad, who hired him to oversee other studios’ use of Marvel superheroes. Feige would later tell THR that, during his time as a Marvel Studios producer until he was named president of production in 2006, he would learn about the various productions and was “thinking always, ‘One day, if I’m in a position of power, I’ll do things this way; I’m going to not do things like that.’ ”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: At the time of his Next Gen selection in fall 2003, Feige was executive vp at Marvel Studios. He had also just executive produced Ang Lee’s Hulk, the Universal summer release that starred Eric Bana as physicist Bruce Banner, who transforms into his green-skinned alter ego when angered. Although THR‘s review praised the film for its “visual energy, genuine artistry and compelling human emotions,” it collected a modest $245 million globally against a $137 million budget. Three years later, Marvel Studios bought back the rights to the Hulk and released 2008’s Edward Norton-led movie The Incredible Hulk. Creative differences between Norton and the studio resulted in Mark Ruffalo taking over the role for 2012’s The Avengers. Ruffalo returns as the Hulk for Disney’s anticipated Avengers: Doomsday, which hits theaters Dec. 18 and stars an endless array of A-listers. The film is the 39th in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, which Feige helped launch in 2008 with Iron Man.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Feige now serves as Marvel Studios president and Marvel chief creative officer — and in 2025, he gave an endowment to USC to establish the Kevin Feige Division of Film & Television Production. When asked to name his job’s greatest challenge on his Next Gen questionnaire, Feige replied: “Expanding and redefining the public’s perception of a ‘comic book movie.’ “

articles.title: Hassett denies report he's leaving White House: 'Not true'

paras.en: National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett on Friday poured cold water on a report that he's expected to leave the White House in the coming weeks.
paras.zh: 周五，国家经济委员会主任凯文·哈塞特（Kevin Hassett）对有关他预计将在未来几周内离开白宫的报道泼了冷水。

paras.en: That report is "not true," Hassett told CNBC's Eamon Javers in a text message.
paras.zh: 哈塞特在发给CNBC的埃蒙·贾弗斯（Eamon Javers）的短信中表示，该报道“不属实”。

paras.en: Semafor reported earlier Friday afternoon that Hassett "has been inquiring about roles outside the administration," even before Republicans' drubbing in last week's midterm election.
paras.zh: Semafor在周五下午早些时候报道称，早在共和党在上周的中期选举中惨败之前，哈塞特“就在打听政府以外的职位”。

paras.en: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, and his counselor David Zervos, are among the names being floated to replace Hassett, according to Semafor, which cited unnamed people familiar with his plans.
paras.zh: 据Semafor援引知情人士透露，财政部长斯科特·贝森特及其顾问大卫·泽沃斯是接替哈塞特的候选人之一。

paras.en: But a White House official told CNBC in a statement later Friday, "There is no factual basis for this reporting."
paras.zh: 但白宫一位官员周五晚些时候在给CNBC的一份声明中表示：“该报道没有事实依据。”

paras.en: "Kevin Hassett is a key member of President Trump's economic team and will continue working to advance President Trump's economic policies," the official said on condition of anonymity to discuss the matter.
paras.zh: “凯文·哈塞特是特朗普总统经济团队的关键成员，将继续努力推进特朗普总统的经济政策。”这位官员在谈论此事时要求匿名。

paras.zh: 在Semafor的报道发布后，Zervos通过电话联系，拒绝置评。
