articles.title: What Seeded Life on Earth? New Research Challenges the Longstanding Theory That Comets Brought the Ingredients to Our Planet

paras.en: The question of how life started on Earth has proven to be almost as enigmatic as finding organisms on alien worlds. A longstanding theory posits that comets delivered the molecular ingredients that kickstarted life when they smacked into our planet during its youth. But new research suggests that this popular scenario is extremely unlikely.

In a study published October 28 in the journal Scientific Reports, researchers ran computer simulations of the celestial mail service and found that successful deliveries would have been rare, if not impossible. While the findings reorient discussions on the origin of life on Earth, they also posit a slightly more likely place where comets could’ve brought biologically useful organic molecules: our next-door neighbor, Mars.

The team investigated the potential delivery of hydrogen cyanide (HCN), a molecule with hydrogen, carbon and nitrogen, that would’ve been made with leftovers from the solar system’s formation 4.6 billion years ago. It has been detected on many comets and can be a precursor for many of life’s essential building blocks, including lipids, sugars and nucleotides. That’s because the carbon-containing, or organic, molecule has an extremely strong chemical bond that can drive subsequent reactions. The bond also makes it very stable, and thus more likely than other organics to survive an impact.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: “So, if things look bad for hydrogen cyanide, then we think it’s going to be much harder for other, more complicated molecules that are more likely to be broken down during these impacts,” lead author Richard Anslow, a planetary scientist who conducted the research at the University of Cambridge in England, tells Science News’ Skyler Ware.

Comets, sometimes dubbed “dirty snowballs,” are masses of frozen gases, rock and dust located primarily in the outer solar system. When their orbit brings them closer to the sun, their materials get heated up and form a glowing head, as well as a tail that streaks across the sky.

And things did indeed look bad. Anslow and colleagues analyzed comet impact simulations, interactions between the atmosphere and comets, and models of the origin and evolution of comets. They found that comets likely wouldn’t have been able to supply enough HCN needed to seed life on Earth.

For starters, the rate at which the so-called dirty snowballs crashed into our planet quickly dwindled during its first 500 million years, so there were few opportunities for one carrying HCN to have landed here. Most of their simulations—54 percent—resulted in zero impacts. The remainder provided at least one collision, though only a “tiny minority” resulted in up to three collisions, Anslow tells CNN’s Jacopo Prisco.

What’s more, when comet strikes did take place, most dirty snowballs traveled too fast and at too sharp an angle relative to Earth’s atmosphere; impact likely would have vaporized any hitchhiking HCN. And even if some molecules survived but landed in the ocean, they would have diluted quickly, probably before any life-related chemistry could take place. “It’s really this sort of high-temperature pressure chemistry happening immediately post impact” that makes HCN less beneficial for prebiotic chemistry, Anslow tells Chemical & Engineering News’ Ana Georgescu.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Still, “we can’t rule out confidently that there was never a successful impact—there could have been one of these fluke impacts,” he tells CNN. But there are also other post-impact criteria that would have had to be met, such as the presence of liquid water nearby and other life-supporting chemicals, he adds.

While this alignment of conditions seems practically impossible on our planet, the researchers suggest it could have been more likely on Mars. Their simulations show that comets had a greater chance of successfully reaching the Red Planet’s surface—due to the planet’s smaller size and thinner atmosphere—when the solar system was young.

“This is not to say it definitely happened on Mars, of course, but suggests it would be unlikely if it happened on Earth and didn’t happen on Mars,” Anslow says in a statement. “Or the other, perhaps more likely, alternative is that it didn’t happen on either planet.”

However, the team did not consider the possibility of HCN undergoing chemical reactions on the comets themselves to produce sturdier biologically relevant compounds before they plunged into Earth’s atmosphere, Queenie Hoi Shan Chan, a planetary scientist at the Royal Holloway University of London who did not participate in the study, tells CNN.

Either way, something must have happened to kickstart the incredibly diverse life forms that now populate our planet. Anslow and his colleagues point to other possibilities, such as asteroids—which were more frequent terrestrial visitors—or precursors simply taking shape on Earth without extraterrestrial support.

articles.title: Astronomers Found a Mysterious Object Orbiting Far Beyond Pluto. It Could Be a New Dwarf Planet Hidden in Our Solar System

paras.en: Matthew Holman, a senior astrophysicist at the Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory, was sifting through data from the Vera C. Rubin Observatory in Chile when something odd caught his eye. Running a custom-made computer program, he and his colleague Kevin Napier had already spotted more than 2,000 little bright dots in the telescope data, corresponding to newly discovered small objects in the distant solar system. But this one was different: It seemed to be big.

Holman managed his expectations. After all, astronomers in the business of finding distant objects are used to disappointment. “We all have ‘found Mars’ … in terms of a false positive,” Holman tells Smithsonian magazine. They find a bright object that seems really big, then, with a closer look, learn that it’s nothing very remarkable after all. “We’re all really cautious when you see something that looks like it’s large.”

Still, this object grabbed Holman’s attention, so he tried to verify it with Napier and Rubin solar system lead scientist Mario Jurić. They found the celestial body in previous photos of the sky throughout the past decade, which helped them zero in on its orbital path—and the more historical data they found, the more confident they became.
“We know that it’s real,” Holman says. “Every time you look at the predicted location, there it is.” They even found it in photographic plates from 1937, stored in the Harvard plate stacks, he says.

The object, called 2026 ED138, is 46 times farther from the sun than Earth is, and it takes 281.1 years to complete an orbit. Now, the central question is whether it’s big enough to be classified as a new dwarf planet, which would put it among the rare ranks of only five other objects in our solar system.

“This is incredibly exciting,” Paul Byrne, a planetary scientist at the Washington University in St. Louis who was not involved in the discovery, tells National Geographic’s Robin George Andrews. “It heralds a new era of solar system and planetary science.”

Dwarf planets are smaller planets that orbit a star and have a nearly round shape, which happens naturally with objects above a certain size, as their gravitational force pulls evenly on all sides. But dwarf planets are not large enough for their gravity to clear their orbital paths of similar-size debris—the eight planets of our solar system, meanwhile, have achieved that feat. (Pluto’s designation was changed from planet to dwarf planet in 2006 for this reason—its orbit is littered with icy Kuiper Belt objects.)
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: ED138 is likely big enough to be round and, therefore, a dwarf planet—estimates for its size currently range from 370 miles to 930 miles across. But astronomers will have to confirm that measurement, and from the object’s brightness alone, that’s impossible. A highly reflective, smaller object, perhaps covered in gleaming ice caps, might appear just as bright as a less reflective, duller body that’s much larger.

Astronomers have two ways to get the required data. They could observe the world in infrared light, which reveals the thermal energy that it emits after being warmed by the sun. “From that you can figure out how big it is, because we know approximately what temperature it should have,” Holman says.

Alternatively, astronomers could watch the dwarf planet candidate pass in front of a star. If they know how much light comes from that star and how fast ED138 is moving, they can calculate the body’s size based on how long it obscures the light.

Holman says people are working on making those observations with telescopes such as the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA). The dwarf planet candidate isn’t extremely easy to see at the moment, he adds, but “in the next few months it will be, and people will try.”

Right now, astronomers recognize five dwarf planets: Pluto, Eris, Makemake and Haumea in the distant Kuiper Belt, and Ceres in the main asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter. Experts have long suspected that there could be more of these objects, but many of them could have highly elliptical orbits that keep them too far away for us to see most of the time. What we observe is potentially the “tip of the iceberg of a few that are in the close part of their orbit,” Holman says. “There must be a lot that we just haven’t yet detected.”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: The discovery also hints at a relatively unexplored area of our solar system—the region that’s in front of the dense, starry core of the Milky Way from our perspective. It’s harder to pick out objects against all the background light in that zone, and ED138 has been traveling through it for the past 25 to 30 years, Holman notes. “There’s a swath on the sky where we really don’t have a good idea of what is there,” he adds.

What’s more, ED138 is in the southern hemisphere’s sky, and a lot of astronomical observations have focused on the northern hemisphere. But Rubin is poised to help change that: The new telescope, which has the world’s largest digital camera and captured its first images last year, is one of several observatories operating out of Chile’s Atacama Desert.
“Rubin is giving us an unprecedented capacity to explore the sky through a combination of speed, depth and precision,” Jurić says in a statement.

“I was surprised that it found such an object so early,” Megan Schwamb, a planetary scientist at Queen’s University Belfast in Northern Ireland and a member of the Rubin solar system operations team, tells CNN’s Jacopo Prisco. “This was not on my bingo card for this year.”

Understanding more about how and where ED138 formed could reveal new details about the early days of the solar system. And its existence offers a clear reminder that surprising objects remain to be found on the fringes of our planetary neighborhood.
“Is there a Mars- or Earth-size or bigger object out there?” Holman says. “That’s not ruled out.”

articles.title: Designed to Be Unsinkable, the World's Fastest Ocean Liner Finally Hits the Ocean Floor. The 53,330-Ton S.S. 'United States' Is Now the World's Largest Artificial Reef

paras.en: On June 29, 1952, a state-of-the-art ocean liner, nearly 1,000 feet long, opened up to the public. Some 70,000 people flooded to its berth in New York City to catch a glimpse of the S.S. United States before it hit the Atlantic for its maiden voyage.

Almost immediately, the liner proved worthy of the intense interest. On July 3, 1952, the S.S. United States reached England in a record-breaking three days, 10 hours and 40 minutes, a speed that has yet to be surpassed to this day by any passenger liner. In its 17-year run, the ship would go on to host numerous notables, including Marilyn Monroe, Walt Disney, Salvador Dalí and even the Mona Lisa, after the painting’s one and only trip to the United States.

On Wednesday, more than 70 years after its record-setting maiden voyage, crowds once again came out in droves to see the legendary liner depart on one last journey. This time, the S.S. United States was heading to the bottom of the sea for a new life as an artificial reef and diving destination in the Gulf of Mexico.

Designed by the prolific 20th century naval architect William Francis Gibbs, the ocean liner represented the peak of post-World War II maritime technology. Over 100 feet longer than the Titanic, the United States contained no wood except the ship’s grand pianos, built with fire-resistant mahogany. “She will have more aluminum in her than Mr. Gibbs cares to say, a design feature that will contribute to the dual goal of strength and relative lightness,” George Horne reported for the New York Times in 1951. “There are other metals that are even more secret.” In fact, its construction was kept entirely out of the public eye.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Throughout the 1950s and ‘60s, the liner completed more than 800 journeys across the Atlantic, carrying more than 1 million passengers, including many celebrities and politicians.

Throughout its 17-year tenure, the S.S. United States carried four presidents: Harry Truman, Dwight Eisenhower, John F. Kennedy and a young Bill Clinton, who took it to study at Oxford University as a Rhodes Scholar in 1968.
With its intricately designed interior featuring patriotic art, amenities including a movie theater and its unparalleled speed, the S.S. United States provided many passengers with lasting memories.

“The ship going at this incredible speed—it was almost dangerous sometimes for a kid my size to go out on the deck,” Warren Jones, a board member for the nonprofit S.S. United States Conservancy who sailed on the liner as a child, tells FOX Weather’s Julian Atienza and Brandy Campbell. “Those engines, you felt the vibrations and sailed past the Statue of Liberty. It was unforgettable.”

But as airline travel became more accessible, the age of luxury ocean liners soon drew to a close. In 1969, the S.S. United States was abruptly decommissioned. Even crew members were shocked by its sudden withdrawal from service. Several left personal belongings on board, assuming they would go back to work the next day, only to show up to locked gangway doors.
For the next nine years, it languished as a reserve ship for the U.S. Navy, ready to for action if the need arose. But there was no need, and in 1978, the ship was put up for sale.

In the following decades, the ship passed from port to port, from owner to owner, each with different plans for the ship: floating condominiums, hazardous waste removal in Ukraine, a revived cruise liner. But no idea garnered enough money or momentum to last. By 2024, the ship had foundered on a Philadelphia pier for decades.

When the pier’s landlord raised the daily dockage fee to $1,700—$620,500 per year—the S.S. United States was evicted and faced the possibility of getting scrapped. Instead, Florida’s Okaloosa County purchased the ship for $1 million, with plans to turn it into the world’s largest artificial reef. The county already has a fleet of sunken ships off its coast, but the S.S. United States is its crowning jewel.
Officials expect the liner-turned-reef will become home to a variety of marine species, including red snapper, grouper, amberjack, mackerel and tuna. The ship will also be open to divers.

“She’s being reefed and will remain intact and will become a vibrant and dynamic marine habitat,” Susan Gibbs, the conservancy’s president and granddaughter of the ship’s designer, tells the Guardian’s Richard Luscombe.

The conservancy plans to run a museum adjacent to the pier where diving expeditions will set out, featuring the ship’s iconic smokestacks, alongside other parts of the ship’s interior and a collection of artifacts and memorabilia.

Unlike the liner’s legendary maiden voyage, the trip from Philadelphia to the ocean floor was far from speedy. After a handful of false starts and a last-ditch lawsuit, it took months of preparation at a port in Alabama to ready the vessel for its voyage to the bottom of the sea, the New York Times’ Jesse Pesta reports.

Workers removed the ship’s wiring, ductwork, glass and anything that could potentially pose a danger to divers or marine life. They also cut strategic passages through the ship’s interior to create open pathways that would reduce stagnant water and enable divers to easily pass in and out. Finally, they removed off the ship’s two iconic, six-story smokestacks, earmarked for the future museum. The S.S. United States was finally ready for sinking.
On Wednesday afternoon, the ship set out from Destin, Florida. A crew cut holes in the ship and removed more than 400 portholes. Water flooded in, but as night descended, it still hadn’t sunk.
“She was designed to be unsinkable, and that fact has definitely given our crews some challenges today,” Nick Tomecek, a spokesperson for Okaloosa County, told ABC 6.
Or, as William Francis Gibbs once bragged, “You can’t set her on fire, you can’t sink her and you can’t catch her.”

But in the end, only two of those bold claims held true. At 8:59 p.m. Central time, the S.S. United States slipped below the waves, starting a new chapter as a home for marine life and a destination for divers from across the world.

articles.title: Four Turkish soldiers killed in helicopter crash

paras.en: Nov. 12 (UPI) -- Four Turkish soldiers were killed Thursday when a military helicopter they were aboard crashed in the eastern province of Malatya, the Turkish Ministry of Defense said.
The ministry described the crash as an "accident," the cause of which had yet to be determined.

"We pray that God will have mercy on our martyrs and offer our condolences and prayers for strength to their grieving families, the Turkish Armed Forces and our noble nation," the ministry said in a statement.
The four victims were identified by the ministry as helicopter technicians Serkan Önder and Hüseyin Zehir and pilots Majs. Erdem Çimen and Orhun Pinar.
Presidential Communications Director Burhanettin Duran expressed his sympathies in a statement.
"Our condolences to the nation. I pray for God's mercy upon our heroic soldiers who were martyred when our S-70 military helicopter crashed in Malatya," he said.
"I extend my condolences to the grieving families and loved ones of our fallen soldiers and to the Turkish Armed Forces."

articles.title: Van Hollen announces run for Democratic Senate leader

paras.en: Nov. 13 (UPI) -- Sen. Chris Van Hollen announced that he will run for Senate majority leader, challenging Sen. Chuck Schumer for the position.

"In this election, the American people called for change. They called for a change from Donald Trump's disastrous policies -- but even bigger than that, a change from the status quo that isn't working for working people," Van Hollen of Maryland said in a Thursday statement.

"It's now on us to meet this moment, and to do that we need new leadership. This is not about any one person -- it's about answering the call of the American people. That is why I'm running for Senate majority leader."
Schumer, a five-term senator who has led Senate Democrats for nearly a decade, suggested he was open to the contest but that he intends to remain party leader.
"I welcome any discussion about the future of our caucus and the important work ahead," he said in a statement.

"I'm proud of what we've accomplished together -- 55 seats and counting is an amazing result -- and I have the votes to continue serving as Democratic leader. I look forward to leading our new Democratic majority and delivering for the American people."

An established New York City politician, Schumer became Senate Democratic leader in 2017 after running unopposed to succeed retiring Sen. Harry Reid in November 2016. He became Senate majority leader in 2021 when Democrats regained control of the upper chamber, but has served as minority leader since 2025, when Republicans regained the majority.

Van Hollen's challenge comes on the heels of sweeping Democratic midterm victories in which the party flipped at least 44 Republican-held House seats and eight Senate seats to gain control of both chambers of Congress.
Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif., who was among the first to call for new leadership, was quick to voice his support for Van Hollen after the Maryland Democrat announced his intentions.
In a video statement recorded from a moving car, Khanna called on every Democratic senator to support Van Hollen's campaign.

"Now, with electing Chris Van Hollen, we can have new leadership in the Senate," he said, stating Van Hollen would end funding for the Iran war, allow a vote on the Medicare for All proposal and deny aid to Israel.
Van Hollen's announcement comes amid divisions among Democrats over the party's leadership and direction despite its sweeping midterm victories.
There has also been growing dissatisfaction with Schumer at the party's helm since March 2025, when he supported advancing a Republican spending bill to avert a government shutdown.
The decision especially bothered the party's progressive members.

Sen. Bernie Sanders, a progressive independent from Vermont who caucuses with Democrats, said Thursday night that he supports Van Hollen to lead Senate Democrats, two days after he had called for new party leadership.
After praising Schumer as a hard worker during a Tuesday press conference, he said he would not support Schumer's re-election as party leader.
He said that the midterm election campaign was about change, and that it was time for "the Democratic Party, in my opinion, to move in a new and bold direction."
Sen. Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich., similarly withheld her support for Schumer, calling for a new generation of Democratic leadership.

"I think whoever wants to run this caucus should come forward with a plan on how they are going to govern differently, what they're going to do in the first 100 days to put money in people's pockets and in particular how they are going to communicate differently," she said.
She stated that she wasn't seeking party leadership, that what she sought is change and that whoever wants her vote must show "a concrete plan" that is different from the one the party has had.
"I'm a 'no' until and unless I see that from anyone," she said.
Sen. Angus King, an independent from Maine who caucuses with the Democrats, was among those who made his support public for Schumer's leadership.
"Why would you fire the manager when you just won the World Series?" he said in a statement.

articles.title: U.S. disrupts North Korean fake video scheme tied to $400 million theft

paras.en: SEOUL, Nov. 13 (UPI) -- The U.S. Department of Justice said Thursday that it had disrupted a fake video call scheme used by North Korean hackers to steal more than $400 million in cryptocurrency over the past 18 months.
The department also obtained court approval to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion in cryptocurrency stolen from exchange Binance in a separate attack, the largest such heist in history.
The FBI seized cloud infrastructure used in the fake video call scheme, which the agency calls "FaceStealer," including more than 900 webcam videos of victims, the DOJ said in a press release.

Under the ploy, hackers invite targets to video meetings using communication and social media accounts stolen from earlier victims. During the calls, they play prerecorded webcam videos of people known to the target to make the meetings appear genuine.
The hackers also use AI-generated deepfake videos of prominent figures in the cryptocurrency industry to gain targets' trust, the DOJ said.
They then claim there is a technical problem, such as the target's microphone not working, and provide a link or prompt for a "fix" that secretly installs malware.

Once inside the target's computer, the hackers can steal cryptocurrency, take over accounts and access contact lists to identify new victims. In some cases, thefts occurred several months to more than a year after the initial compromise, the department said.
The FBI attributed the sophisticated campaign to North Korean hackers tracked by security researchers under names including APT38, BlueNoroff and Sapphire Sleet.

"North Korea's FaceStealer is a highly effective social engineering scheme capable of deceiving even the most experienced technical and security conscious computer user," Patrick Grandy, assistant director in charge of the FBI's Los Angeles Field Office, said.
"If you can't imagine a scenario where you might fall prey to it, you are not thinking creatively enough."
paras.zh: “如果你无法想象自己可能成为受害者的情景，那么你的思维就不够有创造性。”

paras.en: In the separate Binance attack, the FBI said North Korean military hackers known as TraderTraitor stole some $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency on Oct. 29.
North Korea denied responsibility last week, calling the accusation a "grave political provocation."

Since the theft, collective efforts by the U.S. government and private sector have resulted in the freezing of more than $2.7 billion in stolen assets, the DOJ said. The department has obtained court authorization to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion of that amount.
"By springing into action at a moment's notice, we worked together to freeze this massive criminal fraud in its tracks," U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro for the District of Columbia said.
Binance said Friday that it had fully covered the losses after committing more than $6.34 billion in company funds. The exchange said it was reopening withdrawals in phases.
Authorities say cryptocurrency theft and fraudulent overseas information technology work are key sources of revenue for Pyongyang's nuclear weapons and ballistic missile programs.

"Cryptocurrency unfortunately has become fertile ground for North Korea to defraud victims and fund its malign activities," First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli for the Central District of California said.
North Korean hackers have been linked to a series of high-profile crypto heists, including the roughly $1.5 billion stolen from Bybit in February 2025.

Blockchain analysis firm TRM Labs reported in July that North Korean-linked hackers stole about $643 million in cryptocurrency during the first half of 2026, accounting for roughly two-thirds of all crypto funds stolen worldwide.
A now-disbanded U.N. panel of experts estimated in a 2024 report that illicit cyber activity accounted for about 40% of funding for Pyongyang's weapons of mass destruction programs.

Last month, the Justice Department announced a separate crackdown on North Korean IT worker schemes affecting more than 70 U.S. companies, including two arrests and the seizure of about 187 laptops and other computer devices.
U.S.-based facilitators allegedly hosted company-issued computers that North Korean workers accessed remotely while posing as legitimate employees.

The Treasury Department sanctioned 10 individuals and one entity on Oct. 28 for supporting the North's IT worker schemes. It said Pyongyang takes most of the workers' wages to help finance its weapons programs.

articles.title: In French Election, Centrists Eye a Judo Star and a Central Banker
articles.author: Mark Landler

paras.en: When Teddy Riner, a judo champion and one of France’s most popular athletes, announced this week that he would run for president, it was less a game changer than a welcome diversion. For all of his appeal, Mr. Riner, 37, is unlikely to win the race to replace President Emmanuel Macron next spring.

Yet his quixotic candidacy reveals a hard truth about France’s presidential campaign. Five months before voters go to the polls, many are eager, even desperate, for a fresh face to upend a race that looks increasingly as if it’s on a glide path to the election of France’s first far-right government since World War II.

The main far-right candidate, Marine Le Pen, has held a commanding lead over all her rivals for months — a lead that has only been reinforced by weeks of protests, marred by violence, that have shaken France. The most prominent center-right candidate, Édouard Philippe, has faded in the polls as the unrest has sharpened the appeal of far-right calls for law and order and left-wing calls for social justice.

Another beneficiary of the upheaval is a far-left firebrand, Jean-Luc Mélenchon, who now appears to be the likeliest candidate to advance into a second round against Ms. Le Pen in France’s two-round system. As things currently stand, French voters would be confronted with a choice between two poles of the political spectrum.

Centrist voters are “afraid of being confronted with a duel between Marine Le Pen and Jean-Luc Mélenchon,” said Jean-Daniel Lévy, deputy director of Toluna France, a polling firm. These voters, he said, are an “orphan electorate,” lacking an inspiring candidate, and are “still looking for someone.”

Raphaël LLorca, an analyst at the Jean-Jaurès Foundation, a left-leaning research group in Paris, said the search for a white knight showed “the panic of the centrist bloc.” He added, “It is clear that the election is slipping away from them.”

articles.title: The End of Russia’s Bravest Newspaper
articles.author: Katrin Bennhold

paras.en: Novaya Gazeta was a newspaper of near-legendary status in Russia. It was the home of the investigative journalist Anna Politkovskaya, whose books in the early 2000s offered a searing account of human rights abuses, wartime propaganda and corruption in Vladimir Putin’s Russia. In 2006, on Putin’s birthday, Politkovskaya was shot and killed in the elevator of her apartment building. Twenty years later, Russia is back at war and Novaya Gazeta has shut down.

On Monday, the paper held its last editorial meeting. One final issue will come out in the next few weeks. I spoke to my colleague Valerie Hopkins, who was there to witness the journalists packing up their offices.

Valerie, Novaya Gazeta, the last big independent Russian media organization, closed its newsroom this week. The paper and its journalists have been under intense pressure from President Vladimir Putin for decades. Why now?

The real miracle is that they lasted this long. We’ve watched the Russian government systematically dismantle any media organization that is critical of the Kremlin and critical of the war in Ukraine. This didn’t happen overnight.

First their website was blocked, so you needed a VPN to read them. Then they lost their media license. Then Putin signed a decree nationalizing their printing presses. Then this spring, authorities raided the newsroom and one of their journalists was detained and put on trial. The paper was added to the list of so-called foreign agents — this kind of Stalin-era term that comes with many limitations on what you’re allowed to do.

articles.title: Tourists Brave a Muddy Jungle Trek to See a Famed World War II Wreck
articles.author: Victoria Kim and Matthew Abbott

paras.en: Halfway through the morning, I’m being tossed around like a popcorn kernel in the back of a troop carrier playing an eclectic medley of Backstreet Boys and Papua New Guinean jams.

We’re traveling along what feels more like a collection of loose rocks, arranged to be roughly vehicle width, than a road. I’ve lost count of the number of river crossings, including one where the water lapped a few inches from the car’s windows. And this is during a dry spell.
Our caravan is headed for an unlikely tourist destination deep in the jungle on Bougainville Island, an autonomous region of Papua New Guinea in the Solomon Sea.

The piecemeal remnants of a Mitsubishi G4M1 — Betty, as the planes were code-named by the Allies in World War II — have remained for some 80 years at the crash site of Japanese Navy Adm. Isoroku Yamamoto. This is the spot where Admiral Yamamoto, mastermind of the Pearl Harbor attack, archvillain to Americans in the war, a respected and memorialized figure to the Japanese, met his end in 1943.

Bougainville was occupied by the Japanese in early 1942, in the months after Pearl Harbor, as the Imperial Navy pushed into the South Pacific, with Admiral Yamamoto at the helm. In April 1943, Allied forces intercepted and deciphered Japanese communication on the admiral’s travels, and American P-38 Lightning fighters gunned down his plane over southern Bougainville, a feat the Americans triumphantly dubbed Operation Vengeance.

articles.title: Daddy Yankee Surprised by Janet Jackson Upon Receiving his POTY Award: ‘Your Music Has Inspired an Entire Generation’
articles.author: Sigal Ratner-Arias

paras.en: If Daddy Yankee got one surprise on Thursday (Nov. 12) while being honored as Person of the Year during the Latin Grammys, it was the reunion with American icon Janet Jackson, with whom he recorded the duet “Made for Now” in 2018.

Jackson attended the awards gala to present the tribute to the Puerto Rican reggaeton singer, offering him heartfelt words: “It takes vision and courage to help change the sound of music and to create new possibilities for artists who come after you,” she said. “His artistry helps bring reggaeton to audiences around the world and open doors for generations of Latin urban artists.”

“Ramon, I once said you have a beautiful soul and a great energy and I’m that then and I need it tonight,” she added using Yankee’s real name. “That spirit is part of what makes your impact reach beyond the music. Tu música ha inspirado a toda una generación (Your music has inspired an entire generation).”

Yankee couldn’t hide his emotion upon hearing those words and reciprocated. “She’s a great inspiration, a colleague, a person with such a kind heart and an impressive legacy, from an incredible family of talent,” he expressed as he took the stage to receive the recognition. “Janet, I love you so much, you know I respect you a lot. When we did that song, it was incredible! It’s one of my favorite songs ever, so I wanna thank you for being here,” he added in a mix of Spanish and English.

Speaking about the genre he helped internationalize, Yankee said: “This was music that started from the bottom, started, as we say, in the underground, where our music was challenged. This started with cassette tapes, on the streets. At one point, even the government thought we were criminals and said we had no future.”
“Today, I want to tell you that my dream was to be a baseball player, but I thank you because now we’re dropping beats in the big leagues of the Grammys,” he added.

Earlier in the evening, he delivered one of the most impressive performances at the ceremony, held at the MGM Grand Garden Arena in Las Vegas, with a medley of some of the hits that made him a pioneer and a giant of reggaeton and urban music, and which had everyone dancing reggaeton. Draped in a massive cape with the Puerto Rican flag, the Big Boss kicked off his show alongside Argentine DJ and producer Bizarrap, with whom he recorded “BZRP Music Session #/66” in 2025.

He also performed “Ella Me Levantó,” “Con Calma,” and “Dura” with Bad Gyal, as well as “BOTZ.” The megahit “Despacito,” which he recorded with Luis Fonsi in 2017 and revolutionized Latin music, was also part of the performance, along with “Lo Que Pasó, Pasó,” “Sonríele,” “Rompe” with Colombian star Feid, and “Pokito” with Indian singer and actor Diljit Dosanjh, before concluding with his anthem “Gasolina.” One of the most impressive moments was marked by the surprise appearance of LL Cool J and French Montana.

paras.en: Yankee was honored as the Latin Recording Academy 2026 Person of the Year in a celebration that began on Wednesday night (Nov. 11) with a grand tribute at the MGM Grand Marquee Ballroom in Las Vegas, with figures like J Balvin, LL Cool J, Feid, Trueno and others revisiting his greatest classics.

In 2022, he announced his retirement from music and his conversion to Christianity, but returned three years later with renewed faith and the commitment to make “music with purpose.” His faith-inspired album Lamento en Baile (2025) includes the lively track “Sonríele,” which reached No. 1 on the Latin Airplay chart last October. He is currently promoting his new studio album, La Postal, featuring collaborations with Cardi B, Myke Towers, Danny Ocean and others, and is scheduled to perform at the Coachella Festival in 2027.

This week, the massive, star-studded Hunger Games soundtrack is out; ATEEZ release its 15th mini-album; and U2 drop its 16th album, Carnaval de Luz, featuring the late Dolly Parton … plus much more.
Check out all of this week’s picks below:
The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping – The Album

Following an emotive lead single from Noah Kahan with “Draw You Out,” songs by Gigi Perez and The Smashing Pumpkins followed. Now, the film’s full accompanying album is out and it’s a whopping 29-songs long, clocking it an one hour and 40 minutes. It features artists including Noah Cyrus, Bella Kay and Stevie Nicks while current chart-topper Ella Langley scored the latest focus track, “Here Then We’re Gone.” The bare and chilling song spotlights the country star’s signature vocals, only stripped back with minimal acoustic production as she reminds us that “we’re all on our way to the end of a song.” — LYNDSEY HAVENS

paras.en: Since debuting in 2018, South Korean boy band ATEEZ have kept fans well fed — as evidenced by the release of the group’s 15 mini album Golden Hour: Part.6. The hard-hitting “UP” would sound right at home soundtracking a high-speed chase scene in an action film as the tension and energy of the song brings listener’s heart rates all the way up, just as intended. — L.H.
U2 feat. Dolly Parton, “Torn” (Kent Wells Version)

Dolly Parton’s soaring voice is gracing music fans once again on this pairing with U2 frontman Bono, in what became Parton’s final recorded vocal before her passing in August. This country variation, from Parton’s producer Wells, received a country radio world premiere earlier this week. Written by Parton, U2 and Johnny McDaid (of Snow Patrol), “Torn” intertwines Parton’s crystalline soprano with Bono’s gritty vocal, as they sing of the pain of fractured familial bonds on lines like, “When halfway seems too far to meet/ Across the table too hard to reach.” Backed by a rich blend of guitars, drums, pedal steel and keyboards, the arrangement gives the performance a striking depth. — JESSICA NICHOLSON

paras.en: Genre-blurring breakout 2hollis shared his new album, Piroutte, mid-week to quick praise. Fans were equally quick to notice Mk.gee co-wrote and co-produced the glitchy “Human After All,” which sounds like a thrilling free fall through discovering ones own emotional depth. Elsewhere, album closer “Daisy” is a crunchy techno-pop track about feeling “so nauseous that I can’t eat or sleep at all/ Can we please just stop it before I go crazy?” As expected from 2hollis, he takes what could have been a classic lovesick song and injects it with new life. — L.H.

The band also shared new single “ACES,” a perfectly melodic yet roaring and rallying cry to “keep the fire alive through tryin’ times/ through the slow decay and rapid decline.” It “ACES” is any indication of more to come, Fall Out Boy sounds fired up and ready to rage on stage. Good timing for that tour. — L.H.

Five years after she gifted the world Temporary Highs in the Violet Skies, enigmatic R&B star Snoh Aalegra has returned with Legendary Love. The three-time Grammy-nominated singer’s fourth studio album finds her mining her own love life for a cinematic, 80s R&B-steeped exploration of near-mythological love. Armed with an all-star cast of contributors, including Babyface, Jimmy Jam & Terry Lewis, Raphael Saadiq, Nile Rodgers, Daniel Caesar, Legendary Love is another winning addition to Aalegra’s catalog. — KYLE DENIS

articles.title: 5 Things You Didn’t See on TV at the 2026 Latin Grammys
articles.author: Jessica Roiz

paras.en: The 2026 Latin Grammy Awards featured many memorable moments, including Rosalía and Milo J as the top winners of the night. The former nabbed song of the year for “La Perla” and album of the year for Lux, and the latter won record of the year for “Niño.”

Additionally, Aria Vega won the highly-anticipated best new artist award, dedicating her award to her mother, her fans, her team, and her native Barranquilla—noting that her win serves as an inspiration to all of the aspiring artists hailing from the caribbean coast of Colombia.

Broadcast live on Thursday (Nov. 12) from the MGM Grand Garden Arena in Las Vegas via Univision, UNIMÁS, Galavisión and with streaming on ViX, the 27th annual awards show also aired head-turning performances from Mon Laferte, Anitta, Grupo Frontera, and Rawayana, to name a few. As well as heartfelt tributes to the late Willie Colón and José Alfredo Jiménez.

One of the evening’s biggest highlights was when Daddy Yankee performed a medley of his hits alongside top-notch artists such as Bad Gyal, Diljit Dosanjh, French Montana, Feid, Jay Wheeler, and LL COOL J. The exhilarating performance came on the heels de the Boricua star receiving the the coveted Person of the Year award on Wednesday night (Nov. 11).

“Never in my life have I felt an emotion as powerful as the one I felt today,” he said in his speech at the invite-only gala. “As I was enjoying the moment and reflecting, I couldn’t believe everything I had built, and it reminded me that these songs are not mine—they belong to you.”

Earlier in the day, the telecast was preceded by the Latin Grammy Premiere via a livestream across the Latin Recording Academy’s digital platforms and social channels, where the majority of the categories were awarded. And while the premiere and awards ceremony were both made accessible to viewers back home, Billboard was at the red carpet and media center capturing all the action you didn’t see on TV or the livestream.
Check out everything you missed from the 2026 Latin Grammys, below:

- Anitta’s a New Woman Anitta won best Portuguese language contemporary pop album for Equilibrivm—a set that has made her a brand new woman. “These songs make me feel relaxed, grateful, and happy… I never imagined people would be moved to tears, given that I’m always shaking my ass!” she jokingly said of her winning album. “We should never forget the past—it was great—but I don’t lack anything now. I’m truly living life.” When asked by a journalist what’s left for her to achieve in her career, the Brazilian star admitted: “I do things for the sheer pleasure of it; I’m financially secure enough to lead a good life. The things I still seek are more internal—places I want to travel to and discover. I don’t have many professional ambitions left, but I really love what I do.”

And while the Argentine duo was all smiles at the carpet for their big night, they also revealed their upcoming gig as an opening act for Harry Styles. “How many wouldn’t like to be there with him?” said Paco at the red carpet, while Ca7riel said the opportunity happened thanks to their great contacts. The duo assured they will take their joy and authenticity to the stage once they hit the road with Styles.

articles.title: Latin Grammys 2026: Rosalía Wins Album of the Year
articles.author: McKinley Franklin

paras.en: Spanish singer Rosalía took home the top prize of album of the year at the 2026 Latin Grammys on Thursday night for her 2025 album Lux.

She opened the 27th annual Latin Grammy Awards, live from Sin City, with an emotive medley of her Lux tracks “La Rumba Del Perdón,” “La Perla” and “Dios Es Un Stalker,” joined by angelic dancers ornamented with halos atop a stage meant to look like heavenly clouds.
It was a reminder of the expansiveness of her album: an offbeat, full-hearted embrace of her classical training through huge orchestral movements, inspired by the lives of female saints.

Her “La Perla” also won song of the year, and during her speech, she thanked Mexico and invited her collaborators on the song, the American urban sierreño trio Yahritza Y Su Esencia, to join her on stage.

Daddy Yankee, the 2026 Latin Grammy Awards’ person of the year and first Latin urbano artist to receive the honor, ripped through his biggest hits an hour into Thursday’s award show, treating the stage like a stadium floor.

It was one for the history books: There were outfit changes, set changes and his native Puerto Rico always at the forefront as he ran through “Ella Me Levantó,” “Con Calma,” “BOTZ,” “Despacito,” “Lo Que Pasó, Pasó,” “Sonríele,” “Rompe,” “Pokito” and, of course, “Gasolina” — joined by Bizarrap, Bad Gyal, Feid, Jay Wheeler, French Montana, LL Cool J and Diljit Dosanjh.

When it came time for Daddy Yankee to receive his honor, it was delivered to him by Janet Jackson “with admiration and respect,” as she said in her speech. When he accepted the award, he concluded by saying “Puerto Rico, recuerda. … Puerto Rico no es pequeño. Pequeño el mapa.” In English: “Puerto Rico, remember. … Puerto Rico is not small. The map is small.”
The award show took place live from Las Vegas’ MGM Grand Garden Arena. It aired live on Univision, UniMás, Galavisión and ViX and hosted by actor, producer and musician Roselyn Sánchez.
For the first award of the night, Pablo Alboran and Backstreet Boys’ Howie D presented Juanes with best pop/rock album for Juanesteban.

Performances were at a high level: Karol G was joined by a full orchestra and 12 Mariachis for her música mexicana ballad “Ese Hombre es Malo.” Mon Laferte broke hearts with her soulful “Femme Fatale.” Silvana Estrada’s “Dime” bridged culture and heritage with her signature Venezuelan cuatro, a four-stringed instrument similar in structure to a ukulele.

Kany García stunned with her acoustic, aflamencado single “La Niña Que Fui.” The Uruguayan-born Jorge Drexler’s rendition of “Las Palabras” felt like theater. And Argentine rapper Milo J performed “Solifican12” and “Gil,” joined by the Latin American folk icon Gustavo Santaolalla.
Carín León brought the house down with “Desde Que Te Tengo,” as did Juanes and Vivir Quintana with “Humano.” Elena Rose was joined by sword-wielding dancers for “Alma.”

Brazilian superstar Anitta did a medley of her “Equilibrium” hits — “Desgraça,” “Choka Choka” and “Meia Noite” among them — an eclectic mix of Brazilian funk, samba, bossa nova, semba, reggae, electronic pop performed in Portuguese, Spanish and English.
Soon after, she was back on stage accepting the trophy for Portuguese language contemporary pop album. She used her speech to shine a light on the Black culture of her native Brazil.

There was a touching tribute to the late ranchera icon, Mexican singer-songwriter José Alfredo Jiménez, produced by Edgar Barrera: The Warning covered “Te Solté la Rienda,” Reik did “La Media Vuelta,” Sofía Reyes and Yami Safdie dueted “Si Nos Dejan” and Camila Fernández brought it home with a big belting “El Rey.” Not soon afterward, she headed back to the stage to perform a full-throated “Serpiente De Cascabel.”

It was the first of two tributes: The second was for Willie Colón, the social activist and Grammy-nominated architect of urban salsa music, who died in February of this year. His son, Miguel Colón, as well as Nathy Peluso and Luis Figueroa and others performed.

Awards were handed out quickly, too. Karol G took home the trophy for urban music album for Tropicoqueta. Xavi won contemporary Mexican album for Dosis, his first Latin Grammy. Fonseca was presented the trophy for contemporary tropical album shortly thereafter for his album, Antes Que El Tiempo Se Vaya.

Best new artist went to Colombian singer Aria Vega, who gave her acceptance speech through tears. This year, the Latin Recording Academy made changes to the category so that only artists with fewer than three albums or 25 singles released were eligible to win.

Most of the evening’s awards were handed out during a pre-televised Premiere Ceremony. That included Bobby Pulido winning the Latin Grammy for best Tejano album for his release Bobby Pulido & Friends: Una Tuya y Una Mía (Vol. 2/En Vivo). Just days earlier, Pulido made history in the U.S. midterm elections by securing a seat in the House of Representatives for the Democrats by flipping a Texas district seat.
“I want to tell you that I’m retiring from music, and I’m leaving with so much gratitude,” he said in his acceptance speech.

articles.title: How London-Based Facialist Keren Bartov Prepped Hollywood for This Fall’s Starriest Soirees
articles.author: Erin Lassner

paras.en: If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, The Hollywood Reporter may receive an affiliate commission.

Lightyears before Hollywood’s obsession with beauty biohacking, Keren Bartov was already using medical-grade, high-tech skin care tools to bring glow-from-within radiance to stars’ visages. Her results were most recently seen on clients Cate Blanchett, Elizabeth Debicki and Mikey Madison, who visited the celebrity facialist’s Notting Hill studio for bespoke facials ahead of the annual Harper’s Bazaar Women of the Year Awards in London on Nov. 5.

The 47-year-old aesthetician also saved A-listers from a cross-Atlantic trip by popping up in LA with her suite of skin-plumping, jawline-snatching devices and her own Keren Bartov Advanced Skin Care serums and creams ahead of the Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show and Academy Museum Gala last month. VS Angels models Joan Smalls, Jasmine Tookes, Elsa Hosk and Amelia Gray beamed with Bartov’s signature glow at the lingerie company’s takeover of Sony Pictures Studios on Oct. 18, as did longtime clients Demi Moore and Mila Kunis at the star-studded Academy fundraiser. She also prepped Kim Kardashian’s skin for her 46th birthday party, and also works with Beyonce and mom Tina Knowles, Julia Roberts, Michelle Monaghan, Eiza Gonzalez, Anya Taylor-Joy and Olivia Wilde, to name just a handful.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: “Before a major event, my goal is for the skin to look its absolute best while remaining calm, balanced and refreshed. The last thing I want is to cause irritation or an unexpected reaction right before a red carpet,” notes Bartov. “I often combine technologies that help improve the appearance of firmness and texture with lymphatic drainage, gentle enzymatic exfoliation and skin care that delivers hydration and radiance.”

In fact, the U.K.-based skin expert has an arsenal of more than 50 technologies — in which she’s invested millions of dollars to ensure only the most state-of-the-art facials — “but the number itself isn’t what matters. It’s knowing when to use each one, in what order and in what combination,” explains Bartov. “I’m always looking for [products] that allow me to achieve more precise results with less aggressive intervention. I never introduce a technology or ingredient simply because it’s new or everyone is talking about it. For me, innovation has to be backed by science, safety and meaningful results.”
